statement_full_latex: \label{SA21-BM-domain} For the corrected class, let \(\mathcal C_f(E)\) denote finite configurations and \(\mathcal C(E)\) all downward-closed conflict-free subsets. Then \[ \mathcal C(E)\cong\operatorname{Idl}(\mathcal C_f(E)), \] where ideals are nonempty directed downward-closed sets. The compact elements are the finite configurations, and the complete primes are \(\downarrow e\). This is the coherent prime-algebraic domain correspondence of \citet[Theorems 8--9, Definitions 17--18, p.~102]{NPW1981}. For the whole-figure disjointness of 156-4 set \[ e\perp_E f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \neg(e\#f)\text{ and }\downarrow e\cap\downarrow f=\varnothing. \] The support ortholattice of finite configurations is canonically isomorphic to the closed double polars of \((E,\perp_E)\), and to the support ortholattice using all configurations. statement_full_latex: \label{SA21-BM-cell-calculus} The relations \(\leq,\ll\) are partial orders with \(\leq\subseteq\ll\). statement_full_latex: \label{SA21-C08} Let $M$ carry free reversal and an immediate incidence relation invariant under simultaneous reversal. Suppose the induced relation on orientation orbits generates a poset $P$. These data arise from a regular CW complex with oriented cells and distinguished positive zero-cell orientations if and only if the following conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item Every principal ideal of $P$ is finite. \item Immediate incidences project exactly to covers of $P$; for each cover $u<v$ and each orientation of $v$, exactly one orientation of $u$ is incident to it. \item For every $x\in P$, $|\Delta(P_{<x})|$ is homeomorphic to $S^{d(x)-1}$ for some integer $d(x)\ge0$. \item The products of the two incidence signs around every rank-two diamond are opposite; at an edge the two vertex coefficients have opposite signs relative to the distinguished vertex orientations. \end{enumerate} The spherical condition implies that the poset is graded and that $d(x)$ is its dimension rank. The theorem allows infinitely many cells, unbounded dimension, and failure of local finiteness. The empty case gives the empty CW complex.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-nontoric-cut} If the cut circles in 67/074 are interpreted as arbitrary embedded smooth, or even analytic, circles, cutting and canonical capping does not always give the asserted antiisomorphisms of pointed caps. The geodesic-cut model used in Theorems~\ref{A1-graph-range} and~\ref{A1-bordered-shadow-range} therefore requires geodesic representatives, or toric compatibility together with equality of the paired hyperbolic boundary lengths. Smoothness alone does not supply these conditions. Toric compatibility without length equality defines the larger, noninjective model of Theorem~\ref{A1-toric-domain}.

statement: For fixed normalization, equal-length geodesic surgery is asserted to be a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto the strict nonnegative-weight support-inequality domain, with open convex downward logarithmic image, invertible tangent map and an equivariant homotopy equivalence into the full tensor bundle, including loop edges.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-graph-range} For the fixed normalization, the unbordered canonical surgery map, with actual toric seam identifications as its phase variables, is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto \[ \mathcal U_\Gamma(Y)= \left\{(q_e)\in\prod_{e\in E}(T_{a_e}Y\otimes T_{b_e}Y)^\times: \sum_e p_e\log|q_e|<K_\Gamma(p) \quad\text{for all }0\ne p\in[0,\infty)^E\right\}. \] Its logarithmic radial image is open, convex, and downward closed. If $E\ne\varnothing$, this is a proper subset of the unrestricted nonzero-tensor fiber. The tangent map of surgery is an isomorphism. As the normalization varies on its fixed graph stratum, these images form an open real-analytic subbundle of the nonzero-tensor bundle. Its inclusion is an equivariant homotopy equivalence, and consequently induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups, including orbifold fundamental groups when finite automorphisms are retained. These conclusions allow loop edges as well as edges between different components.

statement: In the normalized separating four-pointed sphere the exact tensor range is 0<|q|<16, and in the irreducible one-node one-pointed torus it is 0<|q|<1, with every phase occurring and modulus determining the common seam length uniquely.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-small-ranges} For the separating one-node $(0,4)$ curve, normalize each rational component by putting its node at $0$ and its two external markings at $1,\infty$. In the resulting tensor frame the exact range is \[ 0<|q|<16. \] For the irreducible one-node $(1,1)$ curve, put its two branches at $0,1$ and its marking at $\infty$ on its rational normalization. In the frame $\partial_z|_0\otimes\partial_z|_1$ the exact range is \[ 0<|q|<1. \] In both cases every phase occurs and the length is uniquely determined by $|q|$.

This already fails for a four-holed sphere with one separating cut, all five geodesic lengths---the four external boundaries and the cut---equal to $2\pi$. Thus, with the componentwise admissibility just specified, the displayed arrow $MDB\longrightarrow M_{\mathrm{st}}ND$ of 67/076 is not a well-defined map on all objects.

statement: For fixed graph and normalization, bordered equal-length surgery is asserted to identify cut surfaces with the strict support-inequality domain of node tensors and external cap radii, whose gradient inverse recovers every length and cap and whose inclusion is an equivariant homotopy equivalence.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-bordered-shadow-range} On the fixed graph and normalization, record the nonzero node tensors $q_e$ and the external cap shadows, of radii $r_l>0$. Canonical cutting and capping gives a real-analytic diffeomorphism from bordered cut surfaces, with actual toric seam phases, onto \begin{align*} \mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)=\biggl\{(q,r):\quad& \sum_{e\in E}p_e\log|q_e|+ \sum_{l\in L}p_l\log r_l<K_{\Gamma,L}(p)\\ &\text{for every }0\ne p\in[0,\infty)^P\biggr\}. \end{align*} The logarithmic radial image is open, convex, and downward closed. The source length at every edge or external leg is $2\pi\sqrt{t_j}$, where $t$ is the unique solution \[ \nabla\Psi_{\Gamma,L}(t) =\bigl((\log|q_e|)_{e\in E},(\log r_l)_{l\in L}\bigr). \] Thus the node tensors and the external shadows determine all node and external cap domains, all boundary lengths, and the cut surface. The statement includes self-nodes and fixed cusp markings. Its tangent map is an isomorphism; as the normalization varies, the range forms an open real-analytic subbundle. The inclusion into the full nonzero-tensor and positive-shadow bundle is an equivariant homotopy equivalence.

statement: When arbitrary embedded external discs are retained, a tuple lies in the canonical geodesic surgery image exactly when its tensors and radii satisfy the support inequalities and its full disc shapes equal those of the uniquely recovered canonical cap system.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-bordered-shape-image} Replace the manuscript's external-only admissibility requirement by arbitrary embedded pointed external discs with disjoint analytic closures avoiding every other special point. The exact image of canonical surgery in this target consists of the tuples $(Y,(q_e),(D_l))$ satisfying both of the following conditions: \begin{enumerate} \item The tensors and the shadows $r_l=r(D_l)$ satisfy all support inequalities of Theorem~\ref{A1-bordered-shadow-range}. \item Let $t$ be the unique gradient inverse furnished by that theorem. On every component, the given external discs $D_l$ are exactly the external members of the canonical full cap system with squared length parameters $B_vt$. \end{enumerate} These conditions determine a real-analytic graph over $\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$. They give a complete reconstruction criterion, and do not require the retained external subsystem to be admissible after the node caps have been discarded.

statement: Allowing independent toric seam lengths preserves the tensor-and-shadow image but makes surgery a real-analytic projection with an R^E fibre of logarithmic branch-length differences, an |E|-dimensional tangent kernel and an equivariant deformation retraction onto the equal-length geodesic submodel.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-toric-domain} The tensor and external-shadow map from $\mathcal R_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$ has exactly the same image $\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$ as the equal-length geodesic map of Theorem~\ref{A1-bordered-shadow-range}; for $L=\varnothing$ this is $\mathcal U_\Gamma(Y)$ of Theorem~\ref{A1-graph-range}. In particular \[ P_*(D_Y)=\left\{y:\ p\cdot y<K_{\Gamma,L}(p) \text{ for all }0\ne p\in[0,\infty)^P\right\}. \] This is a proper subset of the unrestricted tensor/shadow fiber whenever $P\ne\varnothing$; when $P=\varnothing$ it is the entire one-point fiber. Before finite automorphism quotients, the fiber over a fixed tensor and shadow tuple is an open convex set of dimension $|E|$ in its full cap logarithms. More strongly, after orienting each edge, the quantities \[ d_e=s_{h_e^+}-s_{h_e^-}\in\R \] give a global real-analytic identification \[ \mathcal R_{\Gamma,L}(Y) \simeq\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)\times\R^E, \] under which the surgery map is projection and the geodesic submodel is $d=0$. Thus its tangent map is surjective with kernel dimension $|E|$; it is an isomorphism precisely when $E=\varnothing$. If the normalization varies and the graph has total genus $g$ and $n$ external markings, the broader toric source has real dimension $6g-6+2n+|L|+|E|$, whereas the tensor/shadow target has dimension $6g-6+2n+|L|$. Thus the dimension count in 67/077 applies to the geodesic model, not to actual toric cuts of independent lengths. The identification is intrinsic if $\R^E$ is regarded as the real space of antisymmetric functions on the two branches of each edge. Branch interchange changes the corresponding $d_e$ to $-d_e$, and graph automorphisms also permute edges. The construction varies real-analytically with the normalization and is equivariant. Consequently it defines a real vector orbibundle over the geodesic image when finite automorphisms are retained. Scaling $d$ to zero is a fiber-preserving equivariant strong deformation retraction. The broader toric surgery map therefore induces the same fundamental-group isomorphism to the unrestricted tensor/shadow target, although its tangent map has a nonzero kernel whenever there is a cut.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-toric-noninjective} Even for the unbordered four-labelled sphere with one separating analytic cut, the torically compatible surgery map is not injective. There are distinct such cut objects with fixed normalization and tensor $q=\partial_z|_0\otimes\partial_w|_0$.

statement: With full external disc shapes retained, a toric surgery tuple is realizable exactly when its tensors and shadows lie in the stated range and some logarithmic branch-difference vector reproduces those shapes, so the unrestricted R^E fibre description applies only to the shadow target.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-toric-full-discs} For the broader toric interpretation, retain arbitrary pointed external discs with disjoint analytic closures, in addition to the tensors. Such a tuple $(Y,q,(D_l))$ is a surgery output if and only if its external shadows $r_l=r(D_l)$ and tensors belong to $\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$ and there exists $d\in\R^E$ for which the unique canonical cap system constructed in Theorem~\ref{A1-toric-domain} has external members exactly $D_l$. statement: For a pant with one boundary of length 2πλ and two cusps normalized at 0,1,infinity, the scaled cap coordinate is z+z²/2+[5/16+1/(16(λ²+4))]z³+O(z⁴), and its conformal radius increases real-analytically from 0 to 4.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-pant-third-jet} Let the hyperbolic pant have one boundary of length $2\pi\lambda$, $\lambda>0$, and two cusps. Normalize its capped sphere by placing the cap centre at $0$ and the ordered cusps at $1,\infty$. Let $r(\lambda)$ be the cap's conformal radius, and normalize its unit-disc coordinate $u_\lambda$ to have positive derivative at zero. Then \[ g_\lambda(z):=r(\lambda)u_\lambda(z) =z+\frac12z^2+\beta(\lambda)z^3+O(z^4), \qquad \beta(\lambda)=\frac5{16} +\frac1{16(\lambda^2+4)}. \] Moreover $r:(0,\infty)\to(0,4)$ is a strictly increasing real-analytic bijection.

statement: Plumbing germs g_i(z)=z+z²/2+β_i z³+O(z⁴) gives cross-ratio t−t²/2+[9/16−5(β_1+β_2)/4+4β_1β_2]t³+O(t⁴), with the stated pant germs specializing the cubic coefficient to 11/64+1/[64(λ_1²+4)(λ_2²+4)].

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-four-point-plumbing-jet} On two spheres with node $0$ and external markings $1,\infty$, take node-coordinate germs \[ g_i(z)=z+\frac12z^2+\beta_i z^3+O(z^4),\qquad i=1,2. \] Plumb by $g_1(z)g_2(w)=t$. On the resulting four-pointed sphere, normalize the global coordinate so that the first component's $\infty$ is $\infty$, its $1$ is $1$, and the second component's $\infty$ is $0$. Let $\Lambda(t)$ be the coordinate of the second component's $1$. Then \[ \Lambda(t)=t-\frac12t^2+ \left(\frac9{16}-\frac54(\beta_1+\beta_2) +4\beta_1\beta_2\right)t^3+O(t^4). \] In particular, for the germs of Lemma~\ref{A1-pant-third-jet}, the cubic coefficient is \[ C(\lambda_1,\lambda_2) =\frac{11}{64} +\frac1{64(\lambda_1^2+4)(\lambda_2^2+4)}. \]

statement: Two isotopic analytic cuts of one four-punctured sphere can both be torically compatible yet produce different raw canonical tensors, so raw toric surgery does not descend to cut isotopy classes, unlike surgery after choosing the geodesic representative.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-toric-nondescent} There is a four-labelled punctured sphere $X$ with two isotopic essential analytic cuts $C,C_{\mathrm{geo}}$ such that both cuts are canonically torically compatible, $C_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is the unique hyperbolic geodesic in their isotopy class, and raw canonical cutting and capping produces different nodal tensors. Thus raw toric surgery does not descend to a functor on cut isotopy classes. Replacing a representative by its geodesic before applying surgery defines the different, well-defined functor already studied.

statement: The complex moduli component of four-labelled punctured spheres with one unoriented geodesic cut class is a punctured disc H/<τ↦τ+2>, so it is not the analytification of a smooth finite-type algebraic curve or algebraically isomorphic to the unrestricted tensor stratum C×.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-cut-not-algebraic} Let $\mathcal D$ be a connected component of the moduli space of four-labelled punctured spheres equipped with one essential unoriented cut isotopy class, represented by its hyperbolic geodesic. Give $\mathcal D$ its natural complex structure: forgetting the locally constant cut class is a local biholomorphism to $M_{0,4}^{\mathrm{an}}$. Then \[ \mathcal D\simeq \mathbb H/\langle\tau\mapsto\tau+2\rangle \simeq\{q\in\C:0<|q|<1\}. \] In particular $\mathcal D$ is not the analytification of a smooth connected finite-type algebraic curve over $\C$. Thus the natural geodesic-cut source cannot be treated as a finite-type algebraic moduli curve, and it cannot be algebraically isomorphic to the corresponding unrestricted nodal-tensor stratum $\C^\times$. This is a limitation of that specified algebraic interpretation; it does not infer nonholomorphicity of the surgery map from its real-analytic description.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-kra-comparison} Fix a maximal pants graph of type $(g,n)$ and put $d=3g-3+n>0$. Kra's horocyclic plumbing parameters range in a domain $D$ satisfying \[ \mathbb D_{e^{-2\pi}}^{d}\subset D \subset\mathbb D_{e^{-\pi/2}}^{d}. \] They cover the moduli of surfaces of that type, generally many times. statement: The annulus xy=t has complete hyperbolic core length 2π²/(−log|t|) and the explicit cosecant metric tending to cusp metrics, while Wolpert's global comparison is local in normalization and coordinate data and supplies no global tensor inverse.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-wolpert-comparison} The local family $xy=t$, $0<|t|<1$, is the annulus $|t|<|x|<1$. Its complete curvature-minus-one metric and core length are \[ ds_t^2=\left[ \frac{\pi}{|\log|t||} \csc\!\left(\frac{\pi\log|x|}{\log|t|}\right) \left|\frac{dx}{x}\right|\right]^2, \qquad L_t=\frac{2\pi^2}{-\log|t|}. \] On compact subsets of either punctured limiting branch the metric tends to the cusp metric. For a degenerating family of compact stable curves, Wolpert's Expansion~4.2 compares the global hyperbolic metric with the interpolated cusp/annulus metric; its constants are local in the normalization parameters and coordinate germs. This supplies a metric comparison for plumbing, not a global inverse on normal tensors.

statement: The Earle–Marden 2011 draft identifies peripheral translation sewing ζ=η+τ with zw=exp(2πiτ), giving |t|<exp(−4πh), collar modulus Im(τ)−2h and the same phase-only toric welding after rescaling the two branch radii.

statement_full_latex: \label{A1-Earle-Marden-original} The joint manuscript of Earle and Marden, \emph{Holomorphic Plumbing Coordinates on Teichm\"uller and Compactified Moduli Space}, dated \emph{Draft 8/24/11}, gives the following identification. It is an original author manuscript, recovered from the public archive of Marden's Minnesota papers directory, rather than the distinct published 2012 chapter. The relevant locators are \S4.1.1--4.1.2, pp.~39--40; \S4.5, p.~50; and \S4.8.1--4.8.2, equations~(4.8.1)--(4.8.2), p.~57 \cite{EarleMarden2011DraftA567}. Normalize the peripheral translation to $A(\zeta)=\zeta+1$. Suppose the two disjoint puncture neighborhoods are the quotients of $\operatorname{Im}\zeta>h$ and $\operatorname{Im}\eta<-h$, where $h>0$. For $\tau=a+2si$, $s>h$, the identification $\zeta=\eta+\tau$ becomes classical plumbing \[ z=e^{2\pi i\zeta},\qquad w=e^{-2\pi i\eta},\qquad zw=t,\qquad t=e^{2\pi i\tau}. \] Writing $\rho=e^{-2\pi h}$ and $r=e^{-2\pi s}$ gives the exact bounds \[ 0<r<\rho<1,\qquad |t|=r^2<\rho^2=e^{-4\pi h}. \] The sewn collar is the annulus \[ \frac{|t|}{\rho}<|z|<\rho,\qquad \operatorname{mod}=\frac{1}{2\pi}\log\frac{\rho^2}{|t|} =\operatorname{Im}\tau-2h. \] On its middle circle the sewing is $re^{i\theta}\mapsto re^{i(\phi-\theta)}$, where $t=|t|e^{i\phi}$. More generally, after rescaling by positive $0<r_+,r_-<\rho$ satisfying $r_+r_-=|t|$, put $u=z/r_+$ and $v=w/r_-$. Then the same sewing is \[ uv=e^{i\phi},\qquad t\,\partial_z\otimes\partial_w =e^{i\phi}\,\partial_u\otimes\partial_v. \] Thus the toric boundary welding in Proposition~\ref{A1-welding-plumbing} is exactly this plumbing operation when its full coordinate germs are retained. The normal tensor is its first-order invariant.

statement: A canonically capped pant with a_j=(1+ell_j²/(4π²))/2 has projective Schwarzian a_0/z²+a_1/(z−1)²+(a_infinity−a_0−a_1)/(z(z−1)), forcing the cap's quadratic coefficient to be (a_0+a_1−a_infinity)/(2a_0).

statement_full_latex: \label{A2-schwarzian} Let a hyperbolic pant have boundary lengths $\ell_0,\ell_1,\ell_\infty>0$, and canonically cap it at the three boundaries. Normalize the resulting sphere by placing the cap centres at $0,1,\infty$. Set \[ a_j=\frac12\left(1+\frac{\ell_j^2}{4\pi^2}\right). \] The hyperbolic developing map extends as a complex projective structure to the punctured capped sphere, whose Schwarzian in the coordinate $z$ is \[ T(z)=\frac{a_0}{z^2}+\frac{a_1}{(z-1)^2} +\frac{a_\infty-a_0-a_1}{z(z-1)}. \] If $u$ is any centred unit-disc coordinate on the cap at $0$, write $u(z)=c z(1+bz+O(z^2))$. Then \[ b=\frac{a_0+a_1-a_\infty}{2a_0}. \]

statement: A punctured hyperbolic curve has canonical Hermitian tangent norms from cusp coordinates, horocycle radius exp(−2π/h), and an unrestricted positive decoration bundle that corresponds to the positive-boundary length bundle under capping.

statement_full_latex: \label{A2-cusp-norm} For a compact pointed complex curve $(Y,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, the complete hyperbolic metric on $Y\setminus\{p_i\}$ defines canonical Hermitian norms on $T_{p_i}Y$. If $q_i$ is its cusp coordinate, then \[ ds^2=\frac{|dq_i|^2}{|q_i|^2\log^2|q_i|},\qquad \|v\|_{p_i}=|dq_i(v)|. \] The coordinate is unique up to a constant of modulus one. A horocycle of circumference $h_i$ has coordinate radius $\exp(-2\pi/h_i)$ wherever embedded. Penner's unrestricted decorations, understood as horocycles in the cusp cover and allowing their immersed images, form a principal $(\R_{>0})^n$-bundle. The map which assigns to $X$ the capped curve and decorations of circumferences $\ell_i(X)$ identifies its positive-length bundle with the one in Theorem \ref{A4-grafting}.

statement: Removing disjoint normal collars from a negative-Euler hyperbolic surface produces a conformal factor solving Δu=exp(2u)−1 with outward normal derivative tanh(d_i), and u is positive so the new boundary length exceeds the old length times cosh(d_i).

statement_full_latex: \label{A2-collar} Let $(M,g)$ be a compact hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary and negative Euler characteristic. Remove pairwise disjoint normal collars of widths $d_i>0$ from selected boundary components, without changing the topological type, and call the remaining surface $M'$. Let $g'$ be its conformally compatible hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. Then $g'=e^{2u}g$ on $M'$ with $u>0$. More precisely $u$ is the unique smooth solution of \[ \Delta_g u=e^{2u}-1\quad\hbox{on }M',\qquad \partial_{n}u=\begin{cases}\tanh d_i&\hbox{on a new boundary},\\0&\hbox{on a retained boundary},\end{cases} \] where $\Delta=\operatorname{div}\operatorname{grad}$ and $n$ is the outward unit normal of $M'$. The new boundary corresponding to a former boundary of length $L_i$ has length strictly greater than $L_i\cosh d_i$ in $g'$.
