statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-abelian-duality} Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field with perfect residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and let $A/K$ be an abelian variety with dual $A^\vee$. Regard flat cohomology as a complex of sheaves on the ind-rational pro-\'etale site of $k$, and write $C^{\mathrm{SD}}=R\mathcal Hom(C,\Z)$. Then the Poincar\'e biextension induces an isomorphism \[ R\underline{\Gamma}(K,A^\vee)^{\mathrm{SDSD}} \simeq R\underline{\Gamma}(K,A)^{\mathrm{SD}}[1]. \] In particular Grothendieck's pairing on the two N\'eron component groups is perfect, including its $p$-primary part. For the global version let $X/k$ be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$, let $A/k(X)$ be an abelian variety, and let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A^\vee_0$ denote respectively its N\'eron model and the identity component of the dual model. Put \[ V=T\mathcal H^1(X,\mathcal A^\vee_0)_{\rm div}\otimes\Q. \] Here the subscript means the maximal divisible subsheaf, and $T$ is its full Tate module. There is a canonical distinguished triangle \[ V[-1]\longrightarrow R\underline{\Gamma}(X,\mathcal A^\vee_0)^{\mathrm{SDSD}} \longrightarrow R\underline{\Gamma}(X,\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{SD}} \longrightarrow V. \] The term $V$ cannot be discarded in the theorem over arbitrary perfect $k$.

statement: Smooth proper specialization with geometrically connected fibres surjects on étale fundamental groups and is an isomorphism on prime-to-residue-characteristic quotients, but full invariance can fail in positive characteristic even for elliptic curves.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-specialization} For a proper smooth morphism with geometrically connected fibres over a locally noetherian base, specialization between geometric fibres induces a surjection of \'etale fundamental groups. If the special residue characteristic is $p>0$, it induces an isomorphism on the maximal prime-to-$p$ quotients; in residue characteristic zero it is an isomorphism on the full groups. The assertion of full invariance in positive characteristic is false, even for smooth proper elliptic curves.

statement: Dominant globally generated line bundles on Schubert varieties in G/P have vanishing higher cohomology and surjective restriction of global sections from G/P in every characteristic, including higher-cohomology vanishing for nef bundles on G/P.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-homogeneous} Let $G$ be a connected simply connected semisimple group over an algebraically closed field, $P\subseteq G$ a parabolic subgroup, and $X_w\subseteq G/P$ a Schubert variety. For a dominant character $\lambda$ of $P$, with the convention that $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is globally generated, one has \[ H^i(X_w,\mathcal L(\lambda)|_{X_w})=0\quad(i>0), \] and restriction $H^0(G/P,\mathcal L(\lambda))\to H^0(X_w,\mathcal L(\lambda)|_{X_w})$ is surjective. In particular every nef line bundle on the complete homogeneous space $G/P$ has vanishing higher cohomology. This holds in every characteristic.

statement: Parshin–Beilinson adèles resolve quasi-coherent sheaves on noetherian schemes and give higher local fields along suitable complete flags, while the formal punctured-disc multiplicative loop functor represents maps into smooth separated commutative groups through the specified intermediate Abel–Jacobi functor.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-adeles} Let $X$ be noetherian and $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Parshin--Beilinson ad\`eles give a functorial flasque resolution \[ 0\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow\mathbb A^0(F) \longrightarrow\mathbb A^1(F)\longrightarrow\cdots. \] Consequently the alternating flag complex of global ad\`eles computes $H^*(X,F)$. If $X$ is also reduced, excellent and pure dimensional of dimension $n$, the ad\`ele ring of a saturated length-$n$ flag is a finite product of $n$-local fields with last residue fields finite over the residue field of the final point. For the local-Jacobian part, let $A$ be noetherian, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\mathfrak C=\operatorname{Spf}A[[T]]$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A((T))$. The commutative group functor \[ \mathcal J(R)=R((T))^\times \] on $A$-algebras has a canonical natural bijection \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{S\text{-}\mathrm{gp}}(\mathcal J,G) \simeq G(U) \] for every smooth separated commutative $S$-group scheme $G$. It is implemented by an Abel--Jacobi morphism $U\to\mathcal J_{\rm omb}$ and the canonical extensions of group homomorphisms to this intermediate functor. It is not implemented by a morphism $U\to\mathcal J$.

statement: Holonomic complexes of analytic D-modules satisfy local de Rham–solution duality with the displayed dimension shifts and no regular-singularity hypothesis.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-dmodule} Let $X$ be a complex analytic manifold of dimension $d$, countable at infinity, and $\mathcal D_X$ its sheaf of holomorphic differential operators. For every bounded complex $M$ of left $\mathcal D_X$-modules with holonomic cohomology, put \[ \mathrm{DR}(M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_X}(\mathcal O_X,M), \qquad \mathrm{Sol}(M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_X}(M,\mathcal O_X). \] There is a canonical isomorphism \[ \mathrm{DR}(M)\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{\C_X}(\mathrm{Sol}(M),\C_X). \] Equivalently, with Verdier duality $D_X(-)=R\mathcal Hom_{\C_X}(-,\C_X[2d])$, one has \[ \mathrm{DR}(M)[d]\simeq D_X(\mathrm{Sol}(M)[d]). \] No regular-singularity assumption is required for this local duality.

statement: Riemann–Roch transformations commute with proper pushforward without projectivity, proper pseudo-coherent morphisms preserve pseudo-coherent complexes and preserve perfect complexes under finite Tor dimension, and complex analytic coherent sheaves admit the analogous proper-functorial K-homology transformation.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-riemann-roch} For every separated finite type scheme $X$ over a field there is a Riemann--Roch transformation \[ \tau_X:G_0(X)\longrightarrow\mathrm{CH}_*(X)_\Q \] commuting with proper pushforward and satisfying $\tau_X(E\otimes F)=\operatorname{ch}(E)\cap\tau_X(F)$ for vector bundles $E$. If $X$ is smooth, then $\tau_X(F)=\operatorname{ch}(F)\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cap[X]$. Thus for a proper morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth schemes, \[ f_*\bigl(\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cap[X]\bigr) =\operatorname{ch}(Rf_*E)\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\cap[Y]. \] Neither $X,Y$ nor $f$ is required to be projective. For proper pseudo-coherent morphisms of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, $Rf_*$ preserves pseudo-coherent complexes. If the morphism also has finite Tor dimension, it preserves perfect complexes. This includes proper lci morphisms and nonnoetherian bases. For complex analytic spaces, coherent sheaves likewise have a natural transformation $\alpha_X:G_0^{\rm hol}(X)\to K^{\rm top}_0(X)$ to topological $K$-homology, compatible with proper direct images. On a complex manifold it sends a vector bundle to its Dolbeault $K$-homology class. This includes possibly singular and nonprojective complex spaces.

statement: Over a locally noetherian G-ring base, an étale stack with algebraic-space diagonal, limit compatibility, finite deformation data, effective formal objects, and open versality is an algebraic stack locally of finite presentation.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-stacks} Let $S$ be locally noetherian with G-ring local rings, and let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $S$ satisfying the usual set-size condition. Suppose its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, it is an \'etale stack, and it commutes with filtered limits of affine schemes. Suppose also that its deformation categories satisfy the Rim--Schlessinger fibre-product condition and have finite dimensional tangent and infinitesimal-automorphism spaces, every formal object over a complete noetherian local $S$-algebra is effective, and versality is open in finite type families. Then $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack, locally of finite presentation over $S$.

statement: A finite locally free equivalence relation on an affine scheme has an affine fppf quotient given by invariant functions with finite faithfully flat quotient map, including Artinian schemes and the stated affine-neighborhood extension to nonaffine schemes.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-artinian} Let $R\rightrightarrows U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an equivalence relation of schemes with both projections finite locally free. Write $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and \[ C=\{a\in A:s^*a=t^*a\text{ in }B\}. \] Then the fppf quotient is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$, $U\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite faithfully flat, and $R=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}U$. In particular this applies to artinian $U$; its quotient is again artinian. The same conclusion of schematic representability holds for nonaffine $U$ if every equivalence class is contained in an affine open, as is the case for $U$ quasi-projective over an affine scheme.

statement: A holomorphic self-map with nondegenerate fixed points on a compact complex manifold satisfies the bundle-valued holomorphic Lefschetz formula, and elliptic complexes have the corresponding real-determinant local expression.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-holomorphic-lefschetz} Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold, $E$ a holomorphic vector bundle, $f:X\to X$ holomorphic, and $u:f^*E\to E$ a holomorphic bundle map. Suppose every fixed point $x$ is nondegenerate: $\det_\C(1-df_x)\ne0$. Then the induced maps on coherent cohomology satisfy \[ \sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{Tr}(u\circ f^*:H^q(X,E)) =\sum_{f(x)=x}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(u_x)} {\det_\C(1-df_x)}. \] More generally an elliptic complex on a compact smooth manifold, with a geometric endomorphism over a map having only nondegenerate fixed points, has local contribution $\sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{Tr}(u_{q,x})/ |\det_\R(1-df_x)|$.

statement: An infinity-topos has a pro-space shape and internal homotopy sheaves with fibre-sequence and Hurewicz properties, complex algebraic étale shapes compare after profinite completion with analytic homotopy types, and infinitesimal fppf homotopy sheaves remain distinct from small-étale and external shape invariants.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-homotopy} Every $\infty$-topos $\mathcal X$ has a shape, the pro-space corepresenting the accessible left exact functor $K\mapsto\Gamma_{\mathcal X}(\Delta K)$. A pointed object $A\in\mathcal X$ has internal homotopy sheaves $\pi_n(A)=\tau_{\leq0}\Omega^nA$; fibre sequences give the usual long exact sequence, with the group action interpretation at $\pi_0$. If $A$ is $(n-1)$-connected and $n\geq1$, then \[ \pi_n(A)^{\mathrm{ab}}\otimes M \simeq\widetilde H_n(A;M) \] for every internal abelian group $M$. For a finite type $\C$-scheme $X$, the profinite completion of its \'etale shape is the profinite completion of the singular homotopy type of $X^{\rm an}$. Infinitesimal homotopy sheaves are possible on the fppf site: in characteristic $p$, $B\alpha_p$ has $\pi_1=\alpha_p$. They are not detected by the small \emph{\'etale} site of a reduced scheme. The distinction between internal homotopy sheaves and external pro-homotopy groups of the shape is essential.

statement: A morphism of separated finite-type Z-schemes into a regular target has the stated rational bivariant orientation and dimension-shifted Chow pullback compatible with standard functorial operations, without requiring flatness or an lci source.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-chow-pullback} Let $Y$ be a regular separated scheme of finite type over $\Z$. For each morphism $f:X\to Y$ of separated finite type $\Z$-schemes there is a canonical rational bivariant orientation $[f]$, uniquely characterized by $[f]([Y])=[X]$. For irreducible $X,Y$ it has degree $-\dim_YX$ and gives, in the relative dimension grading, \[ f^*:\mathrm{CH}_k(Y)_\Q\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{k+\dim_\Z X-\dim_\Z Y}(X)_\Q. \] It is compatible with proper pushforward, flat pullback and refined Gysin maps; compositions of orientations agree whenever the intermediate target is also regular. In particular $X$ need not be regular, and $f$ need not be flat or lci. The coefficient field $\Q$ and the finite type hypotheses are retained.

statement: Generically reduced noetherian quasi-excellent characteristic-zero schemes admit functorial regular-centre resolution, while arbitrary-characteristic varieties admit the stated prime-to-ℓ smooth alterations with SNC boundary without claiming birational resolution.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-resolution} Every generically reduced noetherian quasi-excellent $\Q$-scheme admits a finite sequence of blowups with regular centres, disjoint from the inverse image of its regular locus, whose final scheme is regular. The construction is functorial for regular morphisms, up to omitting empty blowups. For a separated finite type scheme $X$ over any field $k$, a nowhere dense closed $Z\subset X$, and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, there are a finite extension $k'/k$ of degree prime to $\ell$ and a proper surjective generically finite alteration $X'\to X$ of degree prime to $\ell$, with $X'$ smooth quasi-projective over $k'$ and inverse image of $Z$ the support of a strict normal-crossings divisor. The alteration assertion does not assert a birational resolution in arbitrary characteristic and dimension.

statement: A regular closed immersion of codimension c between regular noetherian schemes satisfies absolute cohomological purity Ri!Λ=Λ(−c)[−2c] for torsion coefficients invertible on the ambient scheme.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-purity} Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of constant codimension $c$ between regular noetherian schemes, and let $\Lambda=\Z/n\Z$ with $n$ invertible on $X$. The cycle-class Gysin morphism is an isomorphism \[ Ri^!\Lambda\simeq\Lambda(-c)[-2c]. \] In particular $\mathcal H^q_Z(\Lambda)$ vanishes for $q\ne2c$; in degree $2c$ it is $i_*\Lambda(-c)$.

statement: Regular base change between noetherian schemes commutes with derived étale pushforward for a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism and coefficients of invertible torsion order.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-regular-bc} In a Cartesian square with $f:T\to S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $g:S'\to S$ a regular morphism of noetherian schemes, let $f':T'\to S'$ and $g':T'\to T$ be the projections. For every \'etale $\Z/n\Z$-sheaf $F$ on $T$, where $n$ is invertible on $S$, the base-change map is an isomorphism \[ g^*Rf_*F\simeq Rf'_*g'^*F. \]

statement: A noetherian excellent scheme with an invertible torsion coefficient and dimension function has a uniquely normalized potential dualizing complex giving constructible biduality, with finite quasi-injective dimension exactly in finite Krull dimension.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-local-biduality} Let $X$ be a noetherian excellent $\Z[1/n]$-scheme with a dimension function $\delta$, and put $\Lambda=\Z/n\Z$. There is a normalized potential dualizing complex $K_{X,\delta}$, unique with its normalization, belonging to $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)$. The functor $D_K=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K_{X,\delta})$ preserves $D^b_c$, and for every $M\in D^b_c$ the canonical map \[ M\longrightarrow D_KD_KM \] is an isomorphism. The complex has finite quasi-injective dimension if and only if $X$ has finite Krull dimension; in that case it is also a dualizing complex in the SGA~5 sense.

statement: For a finite-type morphism to a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme, derived pushforward preserves bounded constructible étale complexes of invertible torsion order without properness or finite Krull dimension of the base.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-finiteness} Let $X$ be noetherian quasi-excellent, $f:Y\to X$ of finite type, and $F$ a constructible \'etale $\Z/n\Z$-sheaf on $Y$, with $n$ invertible on $X$. Then every $R^qf_*F$ is constructible and $R^qf_*F=0$ for all sufficiently large $q$. Equivalently $Rf_*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes. No properness assumption on $f$ or finite Krull dimension assumption on $X$ is needed in this theorem.

statement: Affine finite-type pushforward satisfies the stated support-dimension bound δ(Rqf*F)≤δ(F)−q for constructible invertible-torsion sheaves, implying cohomological dimension at most d for affine d-folds over separably closed fields.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-affine-cd} Let $X$ be noetherian quasi-excellent with dimension function $\delta$, let $f:Y\to X$ be affine of finite type, and let $F$ be a constructible \'etale $\Z/n\Z$-sheaf with $n$ invertible on $X$. Set $\delta_Y(y)=\delta(f(y))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(y))}\kappa(y)$ and $\delta(F)=\sup\{\delta_Y(y):F_{\bar y}\ne0\}$. Then \[ \sup\{\delta(x):(R^qf_*F)_{\bar x}\ne0\}\leq\delta(F)-q. \] For an affine variety of dimension $d$ over a separably closed field, this implies $H^q(Y,F)=0$ for $q>d$.

statement: Proper holomorphic maps preserve coherence under every higher direct image, so coherent cohomology on compact complex spaces is finite-dimensional.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-grauert} For a proper holomorphic map $f:X\to Y$ of complex analytic spaces and a coherent analytic $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, every $R^qf_*F$ is coherent. In particular cohomology of a coherent sheaf on a compact complex space is finite dimensional.

statement: Affinoid rigid spaces identify coherent sheaves with finite modules and have no higher coherent cohomology, proper rigid maps preserve coherence, and admissible formal schemes localized at admissible blowups recover the specified rigid spaces.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-rigid} Let $K$ be complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean valuation. On an affinoid rigid space $X=\operatorname{Sp}A$, finite $A$-modules correspond to coherent analytic sheaves and have no higher cohomology. For every proper map of rigid $K$-spaces, all higher direct images of coherent sheaves are coherent. If $R$ is the valuation ring, taking generic fibre induces an equivalence between quasi-paracompact admissible formal $R$-schemes localized at admissible formal blowups and quasi-paracompact quasi-separated rigid $K$-spaces.

statement: The cited SGA 2 finiteness conjecture for annihilators in local cohomology is false, while noetherian local complete intersections of dimension at least four are parafactorial and the stated height-three local factoriality test holds.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{thm:B3-sga2} The reference is to SGA~2, and its proposed finiteness statements cannot all be recorded as affirmative theorems. In particular SGA~2, Expos\'e XIII, Conjecture 1.1 is false: a local cohomology module of a finite module over a regular noetherian ring need not have finitely generated $I$-annihilator. A precise positive local Lefschetz conclusion is that every noetherian local complete-intersection ring of dimension at least four is parafactorial. Consequently a noetherian local complete-intersection ring that is factorial at every prime of height at most three is factorial.

statement: Algebraic correspondences splitting H⁴ of a smooth projective fourfold into fourfolds satisfying codimension-two numerical–ℓ-adic equality transfer that equality to the original fourfold.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B1b-correspondence} Let $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$ be smooth projective fourfolds over $k$, and suppose $D^2_\ell(Y_i)$ holds. Suppose algebraic correspondences $a_i\in\operatorname{CH}^4(X\times Y_i)_\Q$ and $b_i\in\operatorname{CH}^4(Y_i\times X)_\Q$ satisfy \[ \sum_i(b_i)_*(a_i)_*=\operatorname{id} \quad\hbox{on }H^4(X_{\bar k},\Q_\ell(2)). \] Then $D^2_\ell(X)$ holds. In particular this applies to a generically finite surjective morphism from any $Y_i$ to $X$.

statement: Blowing up a smooth positive-codimension centre in a smooth projective fourfold preserves and reflects codimension-two numerical–ℓ-adic homological equality.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B1b-blowup} Let $X$ be a smooth projective fourfold over $k$, let $Z\subset X$ be a smooth closed center of positive codimension on every component, and let $f:W=\operatorname{Bl}_ZX\to X$. Then $D^2_\ell(W)$ holds if and only if $D^2_\ell(X)$ holds.

statement: The source asserts numerical–ℓ-adic homological equality for all rational cycles on the Fermat cubic fourfold and its smooth projective forms in characteristic different from 3, together with the indicated primitive positivity consequence.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B1b-fermat} Let $\operatorname{char}k\ne3$ and let \[ F=\{z_0^3+\cdots+z_5^3=0\}\subset\mathbf P^5_k. \] For every $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence agree for all cycles on $F$ with rational coefficients. The same holds for any smooth projective $k$-form of $F$. Together with Ancona's numerical Hodge theorem for $F$, this places these fourfolds in the homological-positivity class of Proposition~\ref{prop:B1b-criterion}.

statement: Finite exponential and logarithm polynomials biject nilpotent derivations with algebra automorphisms whose difference from the identity is nilpotent, preserving the nilpotency index.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-exp-log} The maps \[ D\longmapsto \exp D=\sum_{j\geq0}\frac{D^j}{j!},\qquad u\longmapsto \log u=\sum_{j\geq1}\frac{(-1)^{j+1}}j(u-1)^j \] are mutually inverse bijections between nilpotent $K$-derivations of $A$ and $K$-algebra automorphisms $u$ for which $u-1$ is nilpotent in $\operatorname{End}_K(A)$. Both sums are finite. The nilpotency indices of $D$ and $\exp D-1$ coincide.

statement: For a nilpotent ideal, exponential bijects derivations that strictly raise its filtration with automorphisms inducing the identity on the associated graded algebra.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-filtered} Let $I\subset A$ be an ideal with $I^m=0$, where $m\geq1$. Exponential is a bijection from \[ \mathfrak d_I= \{D\in\operatorname{Der}_K(A):D(I^k)\subset I^{k+1} \text{ for every }k\geq0\} \] to \[ U_I=\{u\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(A):u(I)=I, \ \operatorname{gr}_I(u)=1\}. \] Its inverse is the polynomial logarithm. Here $I^0=A$ and $\operatorname{gr}_I(A)=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}I^k/I^{k+1}$. This is the valid replacement of the last corollary of 68/046.

statement: An automorphism has differential order at most n exactly when its difference ideal has vanishing (n+1)st power, and for a nilpotent ideal fixed modulo the identity it is a nilpotent exponential exactly when its action on the conormal module is uniformly unipotent, with the displayed bound.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-differential} For $u\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(A)$ let $J=(u(a)-a:a\in A)\subset A$. For every $n\geq0$, \[ u\text{ has differential order at most }n \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad J^{n+1}=0. \] Suppose more generally that $I^m=0$ and $u$ induces the identity on $A/I$. Then $u(I)=I$ and it induces an $(A/I)$-linear automorphism $\gamma:I/I^2\to I/I^2$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $u=\exp D$ for a nilpotent $K$-derivation $D$ of $A$; \item $u-1$ is nilpotent on the $K$-module $A$; \item $\gamma-1$ is nilpotent on the $(A/I)$-module $I/I^2$. \end{enumerate} If $(\gamma-1)^r=0$, then one valid bound is \[ (u-1)^{m+(r-1)m(m-1)/2}=0. \] In particular this characterizes exactly which differential automorphisms are exponentials, by taking $I=J$. The other differential automorphisms are exactly those with non-unipotent action on $J/J^2$, where unipotent here requires a uniform nilpotence bound.

statement: Scaling the dual-number generator by 2 is a first-order differential automorphism that is not a nilpotent exponential, and square-zero algebras identify the general obstruction with failure of uniform nilpotence of T−1 on an arbitrary vector space.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-other-autos} A differential automorphism need not be an exponential of a nilpotent derivation. On $A=\Q[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, the automorphism $u(\epsilon)=2\epsilon$ has differential order one and is not such an exponential. The assertion in 68/045 that $u$ automatically acts identically on $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ is also false. For any $\Q$-vector space $V$, the square-zero algebra $\Q\oplus V$ has all $\Q$-algebra automorphisms of the form $1\oplus T$, with $T\in\operatorname{GL}_{\Q}(V)$. All are differential of order at most one; precisely those for which $T-1$ is uniformly nilpotent are exponentials of nilpotent derivations. Thus no finite dimensional or semisimple description of the remaining automorphisms is available without additional hypotheses.

statement: A linear map intertwines pointwise exponentials of locally nilpotent endomorphisms exactly when it intertwines the endomorphisms themselves.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-intertwine} Let $M,N$ be arbitrary $K$-modules, let $u\in\operatorname{End}_K(M)$ and $v\in\operatorname{End}_K(N)$ be locally nilpotent, and let $f:M\to N$ be $K$-linear. Then \[ f\exp(u)=\exp(v)f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad fu=vf. \] The exponentials are pointwise finite, mutually invertible linear maps.

statement: For arbitrary module functors, ordinary and formal exponential actions are characterized by the stated nilpotence and natural linear-logarithm extension conditions, with formal fibres equal to translates of the endomorphisms annihilated by every nilpotent scalar.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-functor-criterion} For any $K$-module functor $\mathcal M$: \begin{enumerate} \item The ordinary exponential map \[ \{u\in\mathscr E(K):u\text{ nilpotent}\} \longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,\mathscr E^\times) \] is injective. Its image consists exactly of actions $\rho$ satisfying both of the following explicit conditions: there is a single integer $m$ with $(\rho_R(\lambda)-1)^m=0$ for every $R$ and $\lambda\in R$; and their polynomial logarithms define an $\mathcal O$-linear natural map $L:\mathcal O\to\mathscr E$. Thus this exponential map is bijective exactly when every action satisfies these two conditions. \item The formal exponential map \[ \mathscr E(K)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal N,\mathscr E^\times) \] has image exactly the formal actions $\rho$ for which each $\rho_R(\lambda)-1$ is nilpotent in $\mathscr E(R)$ and the natural map $L_R(\lambda)=\log\rho_R(\lambda)$ extends to an $\mathcal O$-linear natural map $\mathcal O\to\mathscr E$. Nilpotence bounds in this assertion may depend on $(R,\lambda)$. Its fibres, when nonempty, are translates of \[ H(\mathcal M)=\{w\in\mathscr E(K): \lambda w_R=0\text{ for every }R\text{ and every } \lambda\in\operatorname{Nil}(R)\}. \] Consequently formal exponential is bijective exactly when $H(\mathcal M)=0$ and every formal action meets the displayed logarithm and extension conditions. \end{enumerate} These criteria apply to every module functor; they require no quasicoherence assumption.

statement: On arbitrary module functors the formal exponential can fail to be injective and either the ordinary or formal exponential can fail to be surjective.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-functor-counter} The formal exponential need not be injective, and neither exponential map need be surjective, for arbitrary module functors.

statement: For a quasi-coherent module functor, formal additive-group actions correspond uniquely to all endomorphisms and ordinary additive-group actions to locally nilpotent endomorphisms, so restricting the latter to uniformly nilpotent operators is exhaustive exactly when local nilpotence is always uniform.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-qcoh} Let $M$ be any $K$-module and $\mathcal M(R)=R\otimes_K M$. Formal actions of $\widehat{\mathbb G}_a=\mathcal N$ on $\mathcal M$ are uniquely the $\bar e_u$ for $u\in\operatorname{End}_K(M)$. Ordinary actions of $\mathbb G_a=\mathcal O$ are uniquely the $e_u$ for locally nilpotent endomorphisms $u$ of $M$. Consequently the ordinary map with domain only uniformly nilpotent endomorphisms is bijective exactly when every locally nilpotent endomorphism of $M$ is uniformly nilpotent. Finite generation of $M$ suffices for this last property but is not asserted to be necessary. The ordinary classification is stated in \cite[Chapter VIII, Example 2.1 and footnote 1, p.~113]{MilneAGS}.

statement: The rearrangement maximum of positive finitely supported functions bounds convolution suprema, equality is characterized by nested positive superlevel sets after translation and inversion, and majorization is detected by all rearrangement pairings.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-rearrangement} For $f,g\in\R^{(G)}_+$, \[ \sup_{f'\sim f}\sum_x f'(x)g(x)=|f,g|, \qquad \|f*g\|_\infty\leq|f,g|. \] An inner product achieves its rearrangement maximum precisely when every positive superlevel set of one factor is comparable by inclusion with every positive superlevel set of the other. Consequently $(f,g)$ is pr\'etass\'e precisely when there exists $s\in G$ such that the superlevel sets of $f$ and $\delta_s*\check g$ together form a chain. Moreover $f'\prec f$ is equivalent to $|f',h|\leq|f,h|$ for every $h\in\R^{(G)}_+$.

statement: For a convolution-stable family containing indicator functions of every possible positive cardinality, pairwise tassé, arbitrary convolution-majorization monotonicity, and Condition K are equivalent, with three-factor indicator tests sufficient for the converse.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C-K-replacement} Let $S\subset\R^{(G)}_+$ be convolution stable and suppose that for every positive integer $k\leq|G|$ it contains an indicator $1_{A_k}$ with $|A_k|=k$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item Every pair in $S\times S$ is tass\'e. \item For every $n\geq2$, $f_i\in S$ and $f_i'\prec f_i$ imply $f_1'*\cdots*f_n'\prec f_1*\cdots*f_n$. \item Condition $K$ holds: under those hypotheses, $\|f_1'*\cdots*f_n'\|_\infty \leq\|f_1*\cdots*f_n\|_\infty$. \end{enumerate} For the implication from (3) to (1), it suffices to assume only the three-factor instances with third factor $1_{A_k}$. Thus the missing hypothesis in Lead L8 is a genuine convolution-majorization property; chain closure and pairwise optimal suprema alone do not supply it.

statement: The literal cone-system axioms with kernel identified with the elements of order at most two admit data exactly when those elements form a subgroup, equivalently all involutions commute, so every abelian discrete group qualifies without cardinality completeness.

statement_full_latex: \label{C-literal-class} Interpret ${}_2G$ as the subset $T=\{t\in G:t^2=e\}$ with the multiplication inherited from $G$, and retain exactly the draft axioms just stated, without adding cardinality completeness. For a finite or arbitrary discrete group $G$, data satisfying these axioms and $i:T\simeq\ker\rho$ exist if and only if $T$ is a subgroup of $G$, equivalently if and only if every two involutions commute. The construction can have a surjective $\rho$ and at least one nonzero cone. In particular, within the abelian category every finite and every discrete group admits a system in this literal sense.

statement: Orientation-reversing toric gluing of pointed cap boundaries produces the tangent tensor eiθdf₊(1)⊗df₋(1) with modulus the product of conformal radii, while its inverse pairing has reciprocal modulus.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:tensor} \status{Proved.} Let $f_\pm:(\D,0)\to(D_\pm,p_\pm)$ be pointed conformal parametrizations. An orientation-reversing isometry between their boundary circle torsors has the form $\zeta_- = e^{i\theta}/\zeta_+$ on $|\zeta_+|=1$. The induced propagator is \[ q=e^{i\theta}df_{+,0}(1)\otimes df_{-,0}(1) \in T_{p_+}Y\otimes T_{p_-}Y, \qquad |q|_{z_+,z_-}=r_{z_+}(D_+,p_+)r_{z_-}(D_-,p_-). \] The inverse tensor, viewed as a nonzero bilinear pairing into $\C$, has reciprocal modulus.

statement: The unrestricted nodal-tensor targets in type (0,4) contain points outside the capping-and-forgetting image, refuting surjectivity and hence all claimed forms of global isomorphism.

statement: For any fixed stable normalization with a node, tensors obtained from embedded caps are bounded in every fixed Hermitian norm, obstructing the unrestricted tensor target in every positive-complexity stable type, while type (0,3) retains the stated full-disc equivalence.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:alltypes} \status{Proved.} Fix any stable pointed complex curve $Y$ with at least one node. The propagators obtainable from embedded caps on its fixed normalization are bounded in each nodal tangent line, for any fixed Hermitian norms. Thus the unrestricted nonzero-tensor target over $Y$ is never the image of capping. For every stable type with $3g-3+n>0$ this gives a counterexample to a global isomorphism. The sole stable type of complexity zero is $(0,3)$; there are no nodal stable curves of that type, and capping with all three external discs retained is an equivalence.

statement: Arbitrary smooth cuts can mismatch the two canonical hyperbolic boundary torsors and therefore fail to define the asserted pointed-disc anti-isomorphism or tensor functor, whereas geodesic cuts remove this definitional defect.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:arbitrarycuts} \status{Proved under stated interpretation; the hypothesis matters.} If the source on 67/074 includes arbitrary smooth cut circles, the canonical hyperbolic boundary torsors need not be respected by the identification of their two banks. In that interpretation the asserted pointed-disc anti-isomorphism, and hence the asserted tensor functor, is not defined by the stated construction. Restricting to geodesic cuts in the canonical hyperbolic metric removes this problem but does not remove Theorem~\ref{A:04}.

statement: For a fixed stable graph, labelled hyperbolic geodesic-cut surfaces are equivalent to compact normalized components with full admissible cap systems, matched paired lengths, and toric boundary identifications, with welding as inverse and cuspidal external zero discs allowed.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:fullcaps} \status{Proved.} For a fixed stable graph $\Gamma$, consider the following two groupoids: (i) hyperbolic bordered surfaces with labelled disjoint essential geodesic cuts of graph $\Gamma$, with conformal isomorphisms preserving all labels; (ii) their compact normalized components with a full admissible system of pointed cap discs at every half-edge and external mark, equal hyperbolic lengths on paired half-edges, and a specified orientation-reversing toric identification on each paired boundary. Cutting and capping gives an equivalence of these groupoids, with inverse obtained by deleting the node caps and welding the paired boundaries. Cuspidal external components are allowed as zero discs.

statement: Small plumbing equations zw=t give local analytic deformation coordinates after the relevant Dehn-twist quotient and canonical tensor normal directions, without parametrizing the entire global moduli by unrestricted punctured tangent lines.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:plumbing} \status{Known, with the comparison explicitly limited to germs.} For a stable complex curve $Y$ and a multicurve $\Gamma$ representing its nodes, choose holomorphic coordinates $z_e,w_e$ near the two branches of each node and local parameters $u$ for the pointed normalization. For sufficiently small $t_e$, the equations $z_ew_e=t_e$ yield local analytic deformation coordinates after the appropriate Dehn-twist quotient. Their normal tangent directions are canonically the lines $T_{p_e^+}Y\otimes T_{p_e^-}Y$. This does not identify an entire product of punctured tangent lines with the global cut-surface moduli.

statement: Canonical infinite-grafting capping identifies marked hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundaries real-analytically with punctured Teichmüller space times positive boundary lengths, extending continuously to zero lengths and analytically within each fixed cusp pattern.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:grafting} \status{Known, with a proved identification of the manuscript operation.} Let $S$ be a compact oriented surface with $n\geq1$ labelled boundary components and $\chi(S)=2-2g-n<0$. Let $\mathcal T^B(S)$ denote marked hyperbolic surfaces with these boundary components geodesic, and let $\mathcal T_{g,n}$ denote the Teichmuller space of the corresponding punctured surfaces. Canonical capping of 67/061--070, followed by remembering the cap centres, satisfies \[ \Psi=(\operatorname{cap},\ell):\mathcal T^B(S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal T_{g,n}\times(0,\infty)^n \] as a mapping-class-equivariant real analytic diffeomorphism. Allowing some boundary lengths to vanish extends this to a homeomorphism \[ \overline\Psi:\mathcal T^{B,\geq0}(S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal T_{g,n}\times[0,\infty)^n, \] real analytic on every fixed boundary/cusp stratum. No assertion of analyticity across all corner strata is needed here.

statement: The complete punctured hyperbolic metric gives the canonical cusp tangent norm and horocycle formula h=−2π/logρ, identifying the positive-length capping bundle with unrestricted horocycle decorations without identifying actual cap discs with cusp discs.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:cuspnorm} \status{Proved; the norm is the known Wolpert norm.} For a marked compact Riemann surface $(X,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, the complete curvature $-1$ metric on $X\setminus\{p_i\}$ defines a canonical Hermitian norm on every $T_{p_i}X$. A normalized cusp coordinate $q$ has \[ ds^2=\frac{|dq|^2}{|q|^2(\log|q|)^2},\qquad \|\partial_q\|_{\mathrm{cusp}}=1. \] In its embedded range the horocycle $|q|=\rho$ has length $h=-2\pi/\log\rho$. The unrestricted horocycle-decoration torsor is parametrized by $h>0$, with no requirement that all projected horocycles be disjoint. Via $h_i=\ell_i$, Theorem~\ref{A:grafting} identifies the positive-length capping bundle with Penner's decoration bundle. This identification does not send actual cap shadows to cusp discs.

statement: After removing smooth collars, the new geodesic-boundary hyperbolic metric is e²ᵘ times the old metric with the stated curvature PDE and boundary condition, and constant-distance collar removal gives u>0.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:collar} \status{Proved.} Let $(X,h)$ be a compact hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary. Remove smooth open boundary collars so that the remaining surface $X'$ is diffeomorphic to $X$. Let $h'$ be its canonical hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. There is a unique smooth real function $u$ on $X'$ such that $h'=e^{2u}h$, and it is characterized by \[ \Delta_hu=e^{2u}-1\quad\text{on }X',\qquad \partial_{n}u=-k_h\quad\text{on }\partial X'. \] Here $\Delta_h=\operatorname{div}_h\nabla$, $n$ is the outward unit normal, and $k_h$ is geodesic curvature measured toward the interior of $X'$. For collars cut at constant inward distance $a_i>0$ below their embedding widths, $k_h=-\tanh a_i$ on the corresponding new boundary and $u>0$ throughout $X'$. Thus $h'>h$ pointwise there.

statement: Orientation-reversing quasisymmetric boundary gluing of compact bordered Riemann surfaces has a unique conformal realization with quasicircle seams, while conformal removability suffices for uniqueness for more general weldings.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:welding} \status{Known existence theorem, with the category and uniqueness specified.} Let compact oriented bordered Riemann surfaces have finitely many paired boundary circles, and glue each pair by an orientation-reversing quasisymmetric homeomorphism, measured in analytic boundary coordinates. The topological quotient carries a conformal structure which restricts to the given structures on every interior, and its seams are quasicircles. It is unique under the identity on the pieces. More generally, for any given welding homeomorphisms, two realizations are conformally identical if one realization's seams are conformally removable. Rectifiable seams satisfy this uniqueness condition. Quasisymmetry is sufficient for existence and characterizes quasicircle realizations; it is not necessary for existence of arbitrary Jordan-curve weldings.

statement: Cutting a Jordan disc along an attached Jordan arc gives the specified prime-end slit normalization, and the converse uniquely realizes precisely the stated fold-compatible quasisymmetric bank involutions as quasiconformal slit pairs.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:slit} \status{Proved from the welding theorem and prime-end uniformization.} Let $V$ be a Jordan disc and let $I$ be a Jordan arc with one endpoint on $\partial V$ and its remaining points in $V$. Cutting $V$ along $I$ gives a simply connected surface with a prime-end boundary circle. Its Riemann map has the boundary identifications of 67/071--073, with the slit tip and its two access points at the attachment prescribed as the three normalization points. No rectifiability is needed for this cutting assertion. Conversely, let the two designated boundary banks be identified by $\varphi$, and form their bank-exchanging involution $H$: $H=\varphi$ on one bank and $H=\varphi^{-1}$ on the other. Require $H$ to be quasisymmetric in an analytic boundary coordinate on the \emph{union} of the banks, including their common endpoint. This condition has a slit realization which is the image of a straight radial slit under a quasiconformal homeomorphism of a disc. After putting its tip at $0$ and its attachment at $1$ in the unit disc, the normalized realization is unique. Conversely every such quasiconformal slit pair has this welding condition. The correspondence is therefore with this specified class of slit pairs; quasisymmetry on a single bank alone is insufficient at the fold. For a prescribed rectifiable slit the normalized welding is unique, but ``rectifiable graph'' does not supply an existence criterion for an arbitrary interval homeomorphism.

statement: Geodesic cuts and rotational cap identifications are analytic, quasisymmetric, and removable, but smooth arbitrary cuts still need toric compatibility to produce the proposed nodal tensor.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:L5} \status{Proved under the stated geodesic-cut convention.} On 67/074--082, geodesic cuts and the rotational capping identifications are real analytic, hence quasisymmetric and removable. No earlier assertion about arbitrary rectifiable weldings is needed for that construction. If ``differentiable cut'' is taken literally without toric compatibility, the obstruction in Proposition~\ref{A:arbitrarycuts} remains; smoothness alone does not produce the claimed nodal tensor.

statement: Multiplication of boundary lengths defines an intrinsic continuous mapping-class-equivariant nonnegative semigroup action on capped hyperbolic Teichmüller space, analytic on fixed zero patterns, with free transitive positive-fibre action and canonical all-lengths-one section.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:action} \status{Proved from Theorem~\ref{A:grafting}.} The semigroup $[0,\infty)^I$ acts continuously on $\mathcal T^{B,\geq0}(S)$ by \[ a\cdot Y=\overline\Psi^{-1} \bigl(\operatorname{cap}(Y),(a_i\ell_i(Y))_{i\in I}\bigr). \] It is intrinsic and mapping-class equivariant; it is real analytic on each stratum on which the source and target patterns of zero lengths are fixed. The group $(0,\infty)^I$ acts freely and transitively on each positive-length fibre. The all-zero multiplier is the capping retraction. The quotient is $\mathcal T_{g,n}$. The section with all lengths equal to $1$ is canonical.

statement: For a fixed labelled stable normalization with cuspidal external ends, attainable logarithmic node-tensor moduli form the explicit Jenkins–Strebel support-function convex domain, and the length-to-modulus map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism with positive-definite symmetric derivative and unique geodesic-cut lift.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:graph-radius-domain} Let $\Gamma$ be a connected stable graph of type $(g,n)$, with edge set $E\ne\varnothing$. Fix its pointed compact normalization components $X_v$, with every branch and external marking labelled. For an ordinary fibre, retain an identification of the normalization with these fixed objects; merely labelling the special points need not remove their finite automorphisms. All constructions below are equivariant for those automorphisms and also define the corresponding groupoid maps. We first take all external ends to be cusps. At each special point choose a local coordinate, used only to measure radii and tensor moduli. Let $I_v$ be the set of node branches on $X_v$. For $a\in[0,\infty)^E$, define $(B_va)_h=a_e$ when the branch $h$ belongs to the edge $e$; both branches of a loop are included separately. Let $H_v$ be the Jenkins--Strebel support function for these active points, with all other special points kept marked, and put \[ H_\Gamma(a)=\sum_v H_v(B_va),\qquad H_v(0)=0. \] Define the explicit open convex set \[ K_\Gamma=\left\{y\in\R^E: \sum_e a_e y_e<H_\Gamma(a) \text{ for every }a\geq0,\ \sum_ea_e=1\right\}. \] The attainable nonzero node tensors are exactly those with $(\log|q_e|)_e\in K_\Gamma$. Every such tensor system has a unique labelled geodesic-cut preimage, up to the equivalence of Theorem~\ref{A:fullcaps}. More precisely, if $x_e=(\ell_e/2\pi)^2$, the logarithmic modulus map is \[ G_\Gamma(x)=\sum_v B_v^T F_v(B_vx),\qquad G_\Gamma:(0,\infty)^E\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K_\Gamma, \] where $F_v$ is the vector of logarithmic cap radii on $X_v$. It is a real analytic diffeomorphism with symmetric positive definite derivative. In the phase coordinates specified by normalized cap maps, the complete tangent map is block diagonal with blocks $DG_\Gamma$ and the identity on $\R^E$. This is the tangent map on the fixed normalization fibre. When the normalization components also vary, the differential is block triangular with the identity on the normalization-moduli base and this invertible fibre block. In particular the full real tangent map is invertible everywhere on the fixed graph stratum.

statement: On a fixed labelled normalization the geodesic-cut map induces the identity on twist fundamental groups, and its restricted tensor image is a stratumwise orbifold homotopy equivalence with invertible real tangent map, despite failure of surjectivity onto the unrestricted target.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:graph-pi-one} For a fixed labelled normalization with its identification retained, the map on ordinary fundamental groups from the geodesic-cut source to the unrestricted tensor target is the identity $\Z^E\to\Z^E$ in the twist generators, although its image is the proper domain of Theorem~\ref{A:graph-radius-domain}. The analogous statement holds for orbifold fundamental groups when the normalization components vary and their finite automorphisms are retained: inclusion of the restricted tensor domain is a homotopy equivalence on each fixed graph stratum. This is compatible with the everywhere invertible real tangent map. Neither test supplies the missing properness onto the unrestricted target.

statement: With external caps retained, the support-domain radius inversion determines a unique length vector, and a geodesic-cut preimage exists exactly when both its tensor/radius data lie in that domain and its recovered actual external discs match those prescribed.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:bordered-radius-algorithm} The same finite-dimensional inversion determines the image when external caps are retained. Add one positive variable $x_i$ for each positive external boundary, and one output coordinate $\log r_i$ for its shadow. In $B_v$, copy a node variable to each of its two flags and an external variable to its single flag. Then $B^T(F_v)_v$ is a real analytic diffeomorphism onto the strict support domain with support $\sum_vH_v(B_va)$. For specified normalization components, node tensors, and actual external pointed discs, the following is a necessary and sufficient test for a geodesic-cut preimage: their tensor moduli and external shadow radii belong to that domain; the unique recovered length vector produces exactly the specified external discs. When both conditions hold, the preimage is unique. Zero external radii are handled on their corresponding face. This test states the additional disc compatibility instead of assuming that forgetting node caps preserves admissibility.

statement: The inverse capping construction satisfies Z₊Z₋=q in normalized canonical cap coordinates that depend on the recovered lengths, without supplying a single fixed pair of plumbing coordinate germs for every tensor.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:cap-plumbing-equation} The inverse on the restricted propagator domain in Theorem~\ref{A:graph-radius-domain} is a plumbing in the canonical cap coordinates, which themselves depend on the recovered length vector. If $z_\pm$ are coordinates at the two node branches and $f_\pm:\D\to D_\pm$ are normalized so that $(z_\pm\circ f_\pm)'(0)=r_\pm>0$, put $Z_\pm=r_\pm f_\pm^{-1}$. Its seam identification is exactly \[ Z_+Z_-=q,\qquad q=r_+r_-e^{i\theta}. \] This identity does not identify the radius inverse with plumbing in one fixed pair of coordinate germs for all $q$.

statement: For two infinite-grafting cap systems on the same connected compact marked Riemann surface, agreement of one embedded pointed cap forces equality of every positive boundary length and, under the usual marking convention, of the complete systems.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:single-cap-all-lengths} Let $(X;p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ be a fixed connected compact marked Riemann surface. Suppose two systems of pairwise disjoint embedded pointed discs $(D_j,p_j)$ and $(D'_j,p_j)$ arise by infinite grafting of hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundaries of positive lengths $\ell_j$ and $\ell'_j$, respectively. If, for one index $i$, \[ D_i=D'_i, \] then $\ell_j=\ell'_j$ for every $j$, including $j=i$. With the usual marking convention, Mondello's grafting theorem further implies that the two complete systems are equal.

statement: The single-cap uniqueness assertion persists when other ends are cusps of length zero, so an unchanged positive cap prevents replacing another positive boundary by a cusp on the same marked compactification.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:single-cap-with-cusps} The preceding uniqueness holds also when some of the other ends are complete hyperbolic cusps, assigned length zero, while the compared cap is a positive cap in both constructions. Therefore keeping one positive pointed cap unchanged cannot be compatible with replacing any other positive geodesic boundary by a complete cusp on the same marked compactification.

Under this convention, the proposed capping-and-forgetting operation $MDB_{g,n}\to M_{\mathrm{st}}ND_{g,n}$ need not take values in its stated target. It already fails for two positive-boundary pairs of pants glued along one boundary, giving type $(0,4)$. More generally it fails on any normalization component that has both a forgotten positive node cap and a retained positive external cap.

statement_full_latex: \label{C:A2b-injectivity} On every face of the nonnegative boundary-length space, the canonical cap system is determined by its conformal radii. On its positive coordinates the logarithmic radius map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $\mathbb R^I$, and is the gradient of a strictly convex real-analytic function of $x_i=(\ell_i/2\pi)^2$. Changing the local coordinate norms translates the logarithmic radius map by a constant vector and does not change these assertions.

statement_full_latex: \label{C:A2b-support} For $a\ne0$, let $Q_a$ be the unique Jenkins--Strebel differential whose characteristic domains are exactly the punctured discs at the active punctures $\{p_i:a_i>0\}$, with circumferences $2\pi\sqrt{a_i}$; at the inactive marked points it has at most simple poles. In particular no additional characteristic annuli are permitted. Let $D_i^a$ be its characteristic pointed discs and $R_i(a)$ their conformal radii. Then \[ H_X(a)=\sum_{a_i>0}a_i\log R_i(a)<\infty. \] Among disjoint active pointed discs avoiding all the other marked points, equality in this weighted radius inequality holds exactly for the indicated Strebel discs. Their complement is the critical graph, including inactive marked points, and has empty interior. The function $H_X$ is convex, positively homogeneous, and continuous on the whole nonnegative orthant.

statement_full_latex: \label{C:A2b-support-integral} The preceding support value can be evaluated directly from $Q_a$. On an active characteristic disc choose the branch $\sqrt{Q_a}\sim i\sqrt{a_i}\,dz_i/z_i$ near $p_i$, and choose a regular point $b_i$ of its boundary. Then \[ w_i(z)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i}{\sqrt{a_i}} \int_{b_i}^{z}\sqrt{Q_a}\right) \] is its normalized disc coordinate up to rotation, and \[ \log R_i(a)=\lim_{z\to p_i} \left[\log|z_i(z)|- \operatorname{Re}\!\left(-\frac{i}{\sqrt{a_i}} \int_{b_i}^{z}\sqrt{Q_a}\right)\right]. \] Thus the image inequalities use only the unique meromorphic quadratic differential with principal parts $-a_i\,dz_i^2/z_i^2$ whose characteristic domains are precisely the punctured discs around the active marks, followed by these integrals and limits. At inactive marks at most simple poles are allowed; there are no additional characteristic annuli. No elementary expression for its coefficients in every genus is asserted.

statement_full_latex: \label{C:A2b-image} For every stable fixed pointed conformal surface and every nonempty active set $I$, the map \[ F_X:(0,\infty)^I\longrightarrow\mathcal K_{X,I} \] is a real-analytic diffeomorphism. Thus a vector of positive radii $(r_i)_{i\in I}$ is realized by a unique admissible canonical cap system, with all other ends cuspidal, if and only if \[ \prod_{i\in I}r_i^{a_i} <\prod_{a_i>0}R_i(a)^{a_i} \quad\text{for every }a\geq0,\quad\sum_{i\in I}a_i=1. \] Here $R_i(a)$ are computed from the unique Jenkins--Strebel system of circumferences $2\pi\sqrt{a_i}$. The zero radius vector corresponds to the all-cuspidal system. These statements give the whole image on all faces, and injectivity on their union.

statement_full_latex: \label{C:A2b-normal-families} For a fixed index $i$, let $f_m:\mathbb D\to X$ be injective holomorphic maps with $f_m(0)=p_i$ whose images avoid every $p_j$, $j\ne i$. Normalize their derivatives to be positive in the chosen coordinate norm. Their conformal radii have a finite upper bound. Every sequence has a subsequence converging locally uniformly to a holomorphic map; if its radii are bounded away from zero, the limit is an injective holomorphic disc avoiding the other marked points. Nonconstant limits of mutually disjoint discs are mutually disjoint. If the radii converge to a positive value, convergence of the normalized maps to a nonconstant limit is equivalent to pointed conformal kernel convergence of their image domains.

statement_full_latex: \label{C:A2b-strebel-limit} Let $x^{(m)}=(\lambda_i^{(m)})^2$ be a sequence of squared length vectors with \[ s_m=\sum_i x_i^{(m)}\longrightarrow\infty, \qquad a^{(m)}=x^{(m)}/s_m\longrightarrow a, \qquad a_i\geq0,\quad\sum_i a_i=1. \] The canonical cap at every index with $a_i>0$ converges, in the pointed conformal-kernel sense, to its unique Jenkins--Strebel disc with circumference proportional to $\sqrt{a_i}$. In particular, if one boundary length tends to infinity while the others remain bounded, its cap tends to the unique one-weight Strebel slit domain. This is a domain limit on the fixed conformal surface; it does not assert Hausdorff convergence of arbitrary boundary traces.

statement_full_latex: \label{C:A2b-pants-extremes} On $X=\mathbb P^1$ with marks $0,1,\infty$, use coordinates $z,z-1,1/z$ respectively. The one-weight extremal disc at $0$ is $\mathbb C\setminus[1,\infty)$, with radius $4$. For equal weights at $0,1$ and zero weight at $\infty$, the extremal discs are the half-planes $\operatorname{Re}z<1/2$ and $\operatorname{Re}z>1/2$, both of radius $1$. Thus every finite canonical cap system satisfies $r_0r_1<1$, although the individual supremum of each of these radii is $4$. Its image is therefore not a box. The limiting disc at $0$ is the slit domain when $\lambda_0\to\infty$ with the others bounded; it is the indicated half-plane when $\lambda_0=\lambda_1\to\infty$ and $\lambda_\infty$ stays bounded.

statement: Every compact negative-Euler-characteristic hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary admits arbitrarily thin analytic collar removals whose new geodesic-boundary metric is neither everywhere larger nor everywhere smaller than the restricted original metric.

statement_full_latex: \label{C:A2e-nonmonotonicity} Let $(X,h)$ be any compact connected hyperbolic surface with nonempty geodesic boundary and negative Euler characteristic. There are arbitrarily thin open collars of its boundary, with real-analytic inner boundaries, such that the remaining surface $X_t$ is diffeomorphic to $X$ but its canonical curvature $-1$ metric $h_t'$ with geodesic boundary is neither pointwise greater than nor pointwise less than $h|_{X_t}$. More precisely, their conformal ratio satisfies \[ h_t'=e^{2u_t}h|_{X_t}, \qquad \min_{X_t}u_t<0<\max_{X_t}u_t. \] This includes every compact hyperbolic pair of pants and every compact one-holed torus. The new boundaries can converge to the original ones in $C^m$ for every fixed $m$.

statement: In characteristic different from 2, Klein-four subgroups of PGL₂ form one conjugacy class with S₄ normalizers, while their six-point fixed sets recover them uniquely except in characteristic 5, where the map is five-to-one and the stabilizer has order 120.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:octahedron} Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field with $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, let $G=\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$, and choose $i\in k$ with $i^2=-1$. Put \[ V=\{z\mapsto z,\ z\mapsto-z,\ z\mapsto1/z,\ z\mapsto-1/z\}, \qquad S=\{0,\infty,1,-1,i,-i\}. \] Every Klein four-subgroup of $G$ is conjugate to $V$. Its normalizer has order~24 and is isomorphic to $\mathfrak S_4$. The assignments $V'\mapsto N_G(V')$ and $\Gamma\mapsto$ its normal Klein four-subgroup give inverse bijections between Klein four-subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $\mathfrak S_4$, in every characteristic different from~2. The assignment taking $V'$ to the union of the fixed points of its three nonidentity elements is a bijection onto the projective translates of $S$ if and only if $\operatorname{char}k\ne5$. In characteristic~5 it is five-to-one, and the stabilizer of $S$ has order~120.

statement: Four-point genus-zero curves with relabelling are equivalent to a point of the three-punctured projective line indexed by the canonical double-transposition Klein group, including characteristic 5 when that group is retained.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:fourpoint-groupoid} Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic different from~2. For a four-element set $I$, let $V(I)$ be its canonical Klein group of double transpositions and let $J(I)=V(I)\setminus\{1\}$. Let $Z(J)$ be the projective line with its three labelled distinct points indexed by $J$, and write $Z(J)^*$ for the complement of those points. There is an equivalence between the groupoid of four-point curves $(X,I\hookrightarrow X)$, with bijections of $I$ allowed, and the groupoid of $(I,\zeta)$ with $\zeta\in Z(J(I))^*$. This remains true in characteristic~5. The construction retains $V(I)$ and does not attempt to recover it from a bare six-point set.

statement: The unordered four-point genus-zero moduli stack is [U/S₄] with cross-ratio action factoring through S₃ and coarse space Spec R[j], so its coarse affine line does not represent the full groupoid.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:unordered-stack} Put $R=\mathbb Z[1/2,i]$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R[\lambda,\lambda^{-1},(1-\lambda)^{-1}]$. The stack of genus-zero curves with an unordered finite \'etale degree-four divisor is \[ \mathcal M_{0,[4],R}\simeq[U/\mathfrak S_4], \qquad \mathfrak S_4\longrightarrow\mathfrak S_3 =\operatorname{Aut}\{0,1,\infty\}. \] The action factors through the displayed quotient and has kernel $V_4$. Its coarse quotient is \[ \operatorname{Spec}R[j],\qquad j=256\frac{(\lambda^2-\lambda+1)^3} {\lambda^2(1-\lambda)^2}. \] Consequently Lead L7 is correct as a statement about the unordered moduli stack, together with its coarse space, but a groupoid of unordered four-point curves is not represented by the scheme $\mathbb A^1_R$. The stack description in fact descends to $\mathbb Z$; adjoining $i$ and inverting~2 are needed only for the specified octahedral presentation.

statement: Cyclotomically normalized invariant procyclic subgroups without maximality cannot classify finitely many nodes and marks, whereas the stated maximal procyclic criterion detects cusps of smooth hyperbolic curves under the non-Tate cyclotomic hypothesis.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:inertia-maximality} Conjugacy classes of all closed subgroups isomorphic to $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, externally invariant under the arithmetic Galois group and acted on cyclotomically, cannot be in bijection with the finite set of nodes and marked points of a stable curve. This is false even for the smoothing fundamental group of the split stable four-pointed genus-zero curve consisting of two three-pointed lines. For a smooth hyperbolic curve over a field with non-Tate $\ell$-adic cyclotomic character, a correct cuspidal criterion uses \emph{maximal} closed procyclic cyclotomically normalized subgroups with nonzero $\ell$-primary part. It identifies the cusps, not every possible nonperipheral cutting curve.

statement: Essential simple closed curves are peripheral, nonseparating, or separating nonperipheral with finer mapping-class orbits determined by side data, and these geometric types are not three conjugacy classes in a fundamental group.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:three-types} For an oriented surface $S_{g,n}$, the geometric kinds of nontrivial simple closed curve are peripheral, nonseparating, and separating nonperipheral. Some kinds may be absent. Within the separating kind, the mapping class orbit is specified by the genera and puncture sets on the two sides, up to exchanging the sides. Within the peripheral kind, a pure mapping class orbit specifies the puncture. These kinds are not three conjugacy classes in a fundamental group, nor three conjugacy classes of homomorphisms $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)\to\pi_1$.

statement: The split nodal four-pointed genus-zero curve has trivial proper geometric étale fundamental group and rank-two free group after deleting external marks, whereas its smooth four-punctured fibre has rank three, so neither ordinary nodal group is the smoothing group.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:ordinary-nodal-loss} Let $Y$ be the proper split stable four-pointed genus-zero curve in Proposition~\ref{A:inertia-maximality}. Its ordinary geometric \'etale fundamental group is trivial. Removing its four external marks gives a free profinite group of rank~2. A smooth four-punctured genus-zero fibre has free profinite group of rank~3. Thus neither ordinary group can serve as the smoothing group in 67/048.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:log-graphicity} For stable log curves over an algebraically closed standard log point, an isomorphism of their geometric pro-$\Sigma$ groups that intertwines their logarithmic inertia actions and preserves the cuspidal inertia classes induces an isomorphism of the graphs of groups. statement_full_latex: \label{A:tensor-log-comparison} Let $(Y,D)$ be a stable pointed curve over a characteristic-zero field $K$. At a geometric node $e$, write $e^+,e^-$ for its two normalization branches and $L_e=T_{e^+}\widetilde Y\otimes T_{e^-}\widetilde Y$. A Galois-equivariant collection $N_e\in L_e\setminus\{0\}$ defines a stable log curve $Y_N^{\log}\to S_K^{\log}$, with thickness one at every node, and hence an outer action \[ \rho_N:G_K\longrightarrow\operatorname{Out}(\Delta_N),\qquad \Delta_N=\pi_1^{\log}(Y_N^{\log}/\overline S_K^{\log}). \] Here $\rho_N$ is the restriction along $s_t$ of the logarithmic base action. Its geometric group is the profinite fundamental group of a smooth surface of the same type as $(Y,D)$. Over $\mathbb C$ it is the profinite completion of the topological surface obtained by gluing the oriented real boundary circles at the nodes using the phases of $N_e$. The construction depends only on $(Y,D,N)$, not on higher order plumbing coordinates or a choice of smoothing family. After a finite extension splitting the nodes, take two tensor systems $N,N'$ on the same $Y$, and put $\delta_e=N'_e/N_e\in K^\times$. Identify their geometric groups and graphs by choosing compatible roots $\delta_e^{1/n}$ in $\overline K$. In the Dehn-twist coordinates of Hoshi and Mochizuki (2012), Theorem~4.8, the difference of the two outer actions is \begin{equation}\label{A:node-Kummer-action} \rho_{N'}(g)=T^{\kappa(\delta)(g)}\rho_N(g),\qquad \kappa(\delta_e)(g)= \bigl(g(\delta_e^{1/n})/\delta_e^{1/n}\bigr)_n \in\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1). \end{equation} The orientation of each twist is chosen to agree with the Kummer inertia of its smoothing coordinate.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:tangential-anabelian} Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$. Let $(Y,D,N)$ and $(Y',D',N')$ be geometrically connected stable pointed curves of hyperbolic type with a nonzero tensor at every node, and use the tangential groups of Lemma~\ref{A:tensor-log-comparison}. The natural map \[ \operatorname{Isom}_K((Y,D,N),(Y',D',N')) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Isom}_{G_K}^{\mathrm{out}} ((\Delta_N,\rho_N),(\Delta_{N'},\rho_{N'})) \] is a bijection. On the right, isomorphisms are continuous and considered modulo geometric inner automorphisms. If markings are labelled, require their peripheral conjugacy classes to match their labels. In particular the arithmetic outer action recovers the curve, its node and cusp incidence, and the actual nonzero tensors, rather than only their orders or their classes modulo powers.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:polystable-compactification} Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$. Consider strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods $U/K$ that admit a hyperbolic-curve tower whose stages are split and saturated in the sense of Mochizuki (1999, \emph{Extending families}), Definitions~7.2--7.3. In characteristic zero it suffices that the punctures of each stage are disjoint sections and its proper smooth curve admits a full level-$\ell$ structure for some prime $\ell\ge3$. Then $U$ has a canonical proper log-polystable compactification $X_U^{\log}$, independent of the choice of a tower. Moreover \[ \operatorname{Isom}_K(X_U^{\log},X_V^{\log}) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{Isom}^{\mathrm{out}}_{G_K} (\pi_1(U),\pi_1(V)). \] Here the arithmetic groups retain their augmentations to $G_K$, and the outer quotient is by the geometric inner automorphisms. The statement includes $U=(\mathbb P^1_K\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^d$ for every $d\ge1$.

statement: The source constructs a canonical normal projective compactification of a characteristic-zero hyperbolic polycurve by finite étale covering, normalization, and quotient, independent of those choices and functorial in isomorphisms, without asserting log regularity of the coarse boundary.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:polycurve-coarse-compactification} Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $U/K$ be a geometrically connected hyperbolic polycurve: $U$ admits a finite tower of hyperbolic curves, in the sense of Mochizuki (1999), Definition~4.6. No splitness or level structure is assumed. There is a canonical normal projective pair $(\overline U,U)$ over $K$, obtained by the following procedure: \begin{enumerate} \item Choose a connected finite \'etale cover $V\to U$ which, over a finite extension $K'/K$, has a split saturated hyperbolic curve tower. Let $(X_V,V)$ be its polystable compactification. \item Choose a connected finite \'etale Galois cover $W\to U$ dominating $V$, and normalize $X_V$ in $K(W)$, obtaining $Z$. \item Extend $G=\operatorname{Gal}(W/U)$ to $Z$ and set $\overline U=Z/G$. \end{enumerate} The resulting pair is independent, up to the unique isomorphism which is the identity on $U$, of all covers, towers, and field extensions in the procedure. Every $K$-isomorphism $U\simeq U'$ extends uniquely to an isomorphism of these pairs. If $U$ already has a polystable compactification, this procedure returns it. For $K$ finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$ and $U,U'$ strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods, consequently \[ \operatorname{Isom}_K\bigl((\overline U,U),(\overline {U'},U')\bigr) \simeq \operatorname{Isom}^{\mathrm{out}}_{G_K} \bigl(\pi_1(U),\pi_1(U')\bigr). \] The right side retains the augmentations to $G_K$, with geometric inner automorphisms divided out. The normal coarse boundary is not asserted to be log regular; the log-regular normalization $Z$ is retained whenever a log specialization theorem is applied.

statement: A compactification satisfying the stated intrinsic anabelian definition is unique and admits unique extension of every morphism between such interiors, so reconstruction of the interior reconstructs the compactified pair.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:intrinsic-anabelian-compactification} The normal compactification of Theorem~\ref{A:polycurve-coarse-compactification} satisfies Definition~\ref{A:anabelian-compactification-definition}. For an arbitrary smooth $U/K$, a compactification satisfying that definition is unique if it exists. Every $K$-morphism between two interiors having such compactifications extends uniquely to their compactifications. In particular arithmetic isomorphism reconstruction of an interior implies arithmetic isomorphism reconstruction of this pair, without retaining any auxiliary cover.

statement: The source claims that augmented arithmetic fundamental groups reconstruct canonical normal compactifications of hyperbolic polycurves over sub-p-adic fields when at least one dimension is at most four, without choosing towers or split level data.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:polycurve-four-dimensional-anabelian} Let $p$ be a prime and let $K$ be a sub-$p$-adic field: that is, $K$ embeds into a finitely generated extension of $\mathbb Q_p$. Let $U,U'$ be geometrically connected hyperbolic polycurves over $K$, and suppose that $\min\{\dim U,\dim U'\}\leq4$. Write $\Pi_U=\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U)$ and $\Delta_U=\ker(\Pi_U\to G_K)$, and similarly for $U'$. For their canonical normal projective compactifications from Theorem~\ref{A:polycurve-coarse-compactification}, the natural map \[ \operatorname{Isom}_K\bigl((\overline U,U), (\overline {U'},U')\bigr) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Isom}_{G_K}(\Pi_U,\Pi_{U'})/ \operatorname{Inn}(\Delta_{U'}) \] is bijective. In particular every prescribed geometric-inner class of an augmentation-preserving arithmetic group isomorphism is realized by one and only one isomorphism of compactified pairs. No chosen tower, split marking, level structure, saturation, or strongly hyperbolic Artin hypothesis is imposed on these interiors.

statement: For the square of the three-punctured projective line, the log pluricanonical ring is independent of the chosen smooth SNC compactification and its Proj is P¹×P¹, yielding a canonical model despite the ambiguity of arbitrary blowups.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:canonical-log-model-product} For $U=(\mathbb P^1_K\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$, let $(Z,E)$ be any smooth projective compactification with reduced simple normal crossings boundary. The graded ring \[ R(U)=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}H^0(Z,\omega_Z^{\otimes m}(mE)) \] is independent of this choice, under the natural identification as rational pluricanonical forms on $U$, and \[ \operatorname{Proj}R(U)\simeq\mathbb P^1_K\times\mathbb P^1_K. \] Thus the arithmetic interior group recovers this canonical log model, although it does not recover an arbitrary chosen blowup.

statement: Proper fs log-smooth degeneration over a complete DVR identifies prime-to-residue-characteristic geometric covers of the generic trivial-log locus with log-geometric covers of the special fibre after all Kummer base extensions.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:log-specialization-higher} Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$, residue characteristic $p\ge0$, and its standard divisorial log structure. Let $\mathcal X^{\log}\to(\operatorname{Spec}R)^{\log}$ be proper and log smooth, with fine saturated log structures and geometrically connected generic fibre, and let $U$ be its trivial-log locus. Write $s^{\log}$ for the induced log special point. There is a Galois-compatible equivalence \[ \operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U_{\bar F})^{(p')} \simeq \operatorname{KCov}_{\mathrm{geom}} (\mathcal X_s^{\log}/s^{\log})^{(p')}, \] and thus an outer isomorphism of the corresponding fundamental groups. Superscript $(p')$ means finite quotients of order prime to $p$; if $p=0$, all finite quotients are retained. The right side uses log-geometric covers, obtained after all finite Kummer extensions of the base log point, not ordinary covers of the underlying singular special fibre.

statement: The displayed two-generator presentation of SL₂(Z) and three orientation-reversing involution presentation of GL₂(Z) hold with their explicit central and involution relations.
