statement_full_latex: \label{A:SL-GL-presentations} The manuscript's presentations, with the involution relations made explicit, are \[ \operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z) =\langle\sigma,\rho\mid\sigma^2=\rho^3,\ \rho^6=1\rangle \] and \[ \operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb Z) =\langle r_1,r_2,r_3\mid r_1^2=r_2^2=r_3^2=1,\ (r_1r_2)^2=(r_2r_3)^3,\ (r_1r_2)^4=1\rangle. \] In the second presentation all three generators reverse orientation.

statement: The four-punctured-sphere mapping class group is (Z/2)²⋊PSL₂(Z), its pure subgroup is Γ(2)/{±I}=F₂, and the two finite quotient sequences end in S₄ and S₃ respectively.

statement_full_latex: \label{A:four-puncture-MCG} Let $V=(\mathbb Z/2)^2$ and $\Gamma(2)=\ker(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\to \operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb F_2))$. Then \[ \operatorname{Mod}_{0,4}\simeq V\rtimes\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z),\qquad \operatorname{PMod}_{0,4}\simeq \Gamma(2)/\{\pm I\}\simeq F_2. \] The quotient of $\operatorname{Mod}_{0,4}$ by $V$, and also the subgroup fixing one distinguished puncture, are each isomorphic to $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)$. The two exact rows are \[ 1\longrightarrow F_2\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_{0,4} \longrightarrow\mathfrak S_4\longrightarrow1, \] \[ 1\longrightarrow F_2\longrightarrow\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z) \longrightarrow\mathfrak S_3\longrightarrow1. \] The map between their finite quotients is $\mathfrak S_4\to\mathfrak S_4/V\simeq\mathfrak S_3$. In particular $\operatorname{PMod}_{0,4}$ is not $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)$.

statement: For an oriented finite-type surface of negative Euler characteristic, forgetting a newly fixed interior point has point-pushing kernel π₁, whereas on the closed torus forgetting is an isomorphism and point pushing is zero.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:Birman} Let $S$ be an oriented surface of finite type with $\chi(S)<0$, and let $p$ be a newly distinguished point in its interior. Then \[ 1\longrightarrow\pi_1(S,p)\stackrel{\mathrm{Push}}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}(S,p)\stackrel{\mathrm{Forget}}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}(S)\longrightarrow1 \] is exact. The new point must be preserved, even when the other punctures may be permuted. The unrestricted assertion without $\chi(S)<0$ is false; for the closed torus the forgetful map $\operatorname{Mod}_{1,1}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{1,0}$ is an isomorphism and the point-pushing map from $\mathbb Z^2$ is zero.

statement: The extended mapping class group of a closed oriented surface with finitely many marked points admits finite generation and presentation by orientation-reversing involutions, without asserting the same for pointwise fixed nonempty boundary.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:reflection-generators} For an oriented closed surface with finitely many marked points, the extended mapping class group has a finite generating set consisting of orientation-reversing involutions. It therefore has a finite presentation on such generators. This assertion concerns marked points; it is not asserted for a group required to fix a nonempty boundary pointwise.

statement: The source describes GQ actions on profinite tangential Teichmüller groupoids through pants/quilt moves, with genus-zero, elliptic, and cyclotomic local inputs and compatible outer actions whose quilt changes may involve Galois-element-dependent inner factors.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:arithmetic-quilts} For every stable type $2g-2+n>0$, the profinite Teichm\"uller groupoids with the above tangential objects admit the natural $G_{\mathbb Q}$ action in pants/quilt coordinates. Fusing moves are controlled by the action on $\mathcal M_{0,4}$, simple moves by the elliptic moduli problem with a nonzero tangent vector, and local Dehn twists and half-twists by the cyclotomic character. The relations are the usual topological quilt relations, with changes of base object and stabilizers retained. At a fixed quilt this gives a lift to automorphisms of the profinite pure mapping class group; at each Galois element a different quilt changes that automorphism by a specified inner factor. The factor may depend on the Galois element: the assertion is equality of the outer actions, not conjugacy of the two entire representations by one fixed inner automorphism. The resulting outer action is compatible with inclusion of quilted subsurfaces and with filling boundary circles by marked discs.

statement: For the real extended group F̂₂⋊〈c〉 attached to the chosen rational base point of M₀,₄, only 1 and c induce compatible automorphisms from GQ, while the full Galois action naturally acts on the family of conjugate real extended groups.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:real-Galois-obstruction} Let $U=\mathcal M_{0,4}=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\setminus \{0,1,\infty\}$, choose the rational base point $2$, and set \[ \Delta=\pi_1(U_{\overline{\mathbb Q}},2)\simeq\widehat F_2. \] Fix an embedding $\overline{\mathbb Q}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$, write $c$ for its complex conjugation, and let $H_c=\Delta\rtimes\langle c\rangle$, using the action supplied by the base point. This is the arithmetic fundamental group over the chosen real closure, and is the profinite completion of the corresponding extended pure four-point mapping class group. An element $\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}$ has its natural outer action on $\Delta$ induced by an automorphism of $H_c$ preserving $\Delta$ if and only if $\sigma\in\{1,c\}$. Thus the whole $G_{\mathbb Q}$ action cannot be extended to this single fixed real extended group with the indicated compatibility. There is instead a canonical outer action on the family $\{H_{\sigma c\sigma^{-1}}\}_{\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}}$ by isomorphisms between its members. With the chosen rational base point this action can be made strict inside $\Delta\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q}$.

statement: The rectangular and rhombic positive-parameter uniformizations classify pointed real elliptic curves and their two real forms, with modular j invariant under reciprocal parameter and incompatible with the proposed logarithmic formula.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:real-elliptic} Every elliptic curve over $\mathbb R$, with its origin, is isomorphic over $\mathbb R$ to exactly one member of the following two disjoint families, with complex conjugation as real structure: \[ E_a(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+i\sqrt a\,\mathbb Z), \qquad E'_a(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C/ \bigl(\mathbb Z+\tfrac{1+i\sqrt a}{2}\mathbb Z\bigr), \qquad a>0. \] For a fixed complex elliptic curve admitting a real structure, there are two real forms. Except for the square lattice, they are either $\{E_a,E_{1/a}\}$ or $\{E'_a,E'_{1/a}\}$ with $a>1$. For the square lattice they are $E_1$ and $E'_1$. For the hexagonal lattice they are $E'_3$ and $E'_{1/3}$. The corresponding modular functions are \[ j(E_a)=j(i\sqrt a),\qquad j(E'_a)=j\bigl((1+i\sqrt a)/2\bigr). \] In each family $j(a)=j(1/a)$. In particular the guess $j=c\log a$ on 67/097 is false for every constant $c$.

statement: Nontrivial involutions in GL₂ of a characteristic-not-two PID with field quotient modulo 2 have one split class and nonsplit classes indexed by residue units modulo lifted units, giving exactly two classes precisely when the unit map is surjective.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:pid-involutions} Let $k$ be a principal ideal domain of characteristic different from~2 such that $k_0=k/2k$ is a field. Conjugacy classes of $\sigma\in\operatorname{GL}_2(k)$ with $\sigma^2=1$ and $\sigma\ne\pm1$ consist of one split class and a collection of nonsplit classes indexed by \[ k_0^\times/\operatorname{im}(k^\times\longrightarrow k_0^\times). \] There are exactly two classes if and only if the unit map is surjective. For $k=\mathbb Z[(1+\sqrt{-11})/2]$ there are four classes in total: one split and three nonsplit. Thus the struck unit-surjectivity proviso on 67/100 is necessary.

statement: Connectedness and 2-torsion-freeness do not force the eigenspaces of a nontrivial free rank-two involution to be invertible, whereas the stated PID or connected 2-invertible hypotheses do.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:eigenmodule-correction} The attached correction R5, which adds connectedness of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to the rank-two projective corollary on 67/091, is insufficient. Even for a connected commutative 2-torsion-free ring, the positive and negative eigenspaces of a nontrivial involution on a free rank-two module need not be invertible modules. The corollary is valid over a PID, as in Proposition~\ref{A:pid-involutions}; it is also valid over a connected ring with $2$ invertible, provided the involution is neither $1$ nor $-1$.

statement: The two real elliptic families have respectively two and one real components and H¹ equal to Z/2 and zero, with annulus and Möbius-band quotients and a fixed-point-free torsor whose quotient is a boundaryless Klein bottle.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{A:real-topology} For every $a>0$, \[ E_a(\mathbb R)\simeq (\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad E'_a(\mathbb R)\simeq\mathbb R/\mathbb Z, \] as compact real Lie groups. Moreover \[ H^1(\mathbb R,E_a)\simeq\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad H^1(\mathbb R,E'_a)=0. \] The quotient Klein surfaces of the two elliptic groups are respectively an annulus and a M\"obius band. The unique nonzero torsor under $E_a$ has no real points; its complex curve modulo its real structure is a Klein bottle, a surface without boundary. Thus the deletion of ``sans'' on 67/101 must be reversed.

statement: The source claims that a rational codimension-two cycle on a smooth projective connected complex fourfold is numerically trivial exactly when its degree-four Betti class vanishes.

statement_full_latex: \label{B:betti} Let $X$ be a smooth projective connected complex variety of complex dimension $4$. For every $z\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, numerical triviality is equivalent to $\operatorname{cl}_B(z)=0$ in $H^4(X,\mathbb Q)$. Here numerical triviality is tested against every $w\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbb Q}$.

statement: Numerical triviality of a rational Chow class on a smooth projective variety is unchanged by extension of the ground field.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:num-basechange} Let $X$ be smooth projective over a field $k$, let $K/k$ be an extension, and let $z\in\mathrm{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbb Q}$. Then $z$ is numerically trivial over $k$ if and only if its flat pullback $z_K$ is numerically trivial over $K$.

statement: The source claims numerical–geometric-ℓ-adic equivalence for rational codimension-two cycles on every characteristic-zero smooth projective fourfold, with disconnected cases handled componentwise and descended by trace.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:charzero} Let $k$ be any field of characteristic $0$, $X/k$ smooth projective and geometrically connected of dimension $4$, and $\ell$ any prime. For $z\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, \[ z\equiv_{\mathrm{num}}0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{cl}_\ell(z)=0\text{ in }H^4_{\acute et}(X_{\bar k},\mathbb Q_\ell(2)). \] For a smooth projective variety without geometric connectedness the same conclusion holds componentwise after a finite extension, and descends by trace.

statement: Ancona’s cited numerical primitive positivity and Lefschetz standard conjecture do not alone establish all-primes homological–numerical equality, and his stated comparison theorem covers infinitely many primes without refuting conjecture D.

statement_full_latex: \label{B:ancona-scope} Ancona's Theorem~1.3 proves positivity for primitive classes \emph{modulo numerical equivalence}. Its combination with the Lefschetz standard conjecture alone does not give the asserted all-primes homological--numerical comparison. The conclusion stated in Ancona's Theorem~1.6 is comparison for infinitely many primes. This is a correction to the proposed proof, not a counterexample to standard conjecture~$D$.

statement: The source asserts all-primes numerical–ℓ-adic homological equality for rational cycles on abelian fourfolds using Broe’s 2026 preprint as an additional dependency.
