statement_full_latex: \label{B:abelian} Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $4$ over any field $k$ and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Then numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence agree on rational cycles on $A$, in particular on its $2$-cycles. This conclusion uses Broe's 2026 preprint, not only the sources remembered in the prompt.

statement: With an algebraic orthogonal Lefschetz decomposition and nondegenerate divisor block, semidefinite primitive positivity yields codimension-two numerical–homological equality exactly when the primitive form is definite, and the stated abelian domination transfers the comparison.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:criterion} Fix a Weil cohomology theory and let $X$ be a smooth projective fourfold. Suppose its rational algebraic cohomology in degree four admits the algebraic orthogonal Lefschetz decomposition \[ A^2(X)=\mathbb Qh^2\oplus L A^1_{\mathrm{prim}}(X)\oplus A^2_{\mathrm{prim}}(X), \] and suppose the divisor summand has the usual nondegenerate Hodge index form. Assume also that the primitive intersection form is positive semidefinite. Then numerical and homological equivalence agree in codimension two if and only if the primitive form is positive definite. In particular, the argument applies whenever the Lefschetz standard conjecture and the Hodge standard conjecture \emph{on homological algebraic classes} both hold. More explicitly, the \emph{class of applicability of the positivity argument} is the class $\mathscr C_H$ of polarized fourfolds with the displayed algebraic decomposition, nondegenerate divisor block and positive definite primitive block. Within the stated semidefinite setting, membership in $\mathscr C_H$ is necessary and sufficient for this argument to prove the comparison. This class includes all characteristic-zero fourfolds for Betti and $\ell$-adic cohomology, all abelian fourfolds using Theorem~\ref{B:abelian}, and smooth projective fourfolds admitting a finite surjective morphism from an abelian fourfold. This determines applicability of the argument; it is not a claim that varieties outside it fail standard conjecture~$D$. Independently of a positivity formulation, $\ell$-adic comparison in codimension two holds for every smooth projective fourfold $X$ admitting a dominant generically finite morphism $f:A\to X$ from an abelian fourfold, for every prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$.

statement: There is a smooth projective complex threefold with an integral homologically trivial one-cycle for which no nonzero multiple is algebraically trivial, refuting numerical-to-τ equivalence in the original question.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:tau} The original image of cote~66, scan~4, reads $\tau$-equivalence; this is the standard relation defined in Kleiman \cite[\S1.1, p.~362]{BKleiman1968}: a nonzero integer multiple is algebraically equivalent to zero. There is a smooth projective connected complex threefold $X$ and an integral one-cycle $z$ which is homologically, hence numerically, trivial, but for which $mz$ is not algebraically trivial for any integer $m\ne0$.

statement: Pointwise rationally equivalent effective zero-cycle families on a smooth projective complex surface induce equal trace two-forms on every smooth irreducible parameter variety.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:trace} Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex surface and $\omega\in H^0(S,\Omega_S^2)$. If $T$ is a smooth irreducible complex variety and $F,G:T\to\operatorname{Sym}^n S$ are morphisms whose effective zero-cycles $F(t),G(t)$ are rationally equivalent for every $t\in T(\mathbb C)$, then their induced trace forms satisfy $\omega_F=\omega_G\in H^0(T,\Omega_T^2)$.

statement: Generic independent points on the elliptic curve y²=x³−x give an infinite-order Albanese-kernel cycle z on E×E and an algebraically trivial divisor D with D²=2z nonzero.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:square} Let $E/\mathbb C$ be the elliptic curve $y^2=x^3-x$, with origin $O$ at infinity, and put $S=E\times E$. Choose $u,v\in\mathbb C$ algebraically independent over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, choose roots $a^2=u^3-u$ and $b^2=v^3-v$, and set $P=(u,a)$, $Q=(v,b)$. Then \[ z=[(P,Q)]-[(P,O)]-[(O,Q)]+[(O,O)]\in\mathrm{CH}_0(S) \] has infinite order and lies in the Albanese kernel. The divisor \[ D=\operatorname{pr}_1^*([P]-[O])+\operatorname{pr}_2^*([Q]-[O])\in\mathrm{CH}^1(S) \] is algebraically trivial, but $D^2=2z\ne0$ in $\mathrm{CH}_0(S)$.

statement: For every complex elliptic curve, exterior products of degree-zero point differences generate the Albanese kernel on its square, so algebraic triviality of such products does not imply rational triviality.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:alb-kernel} For any complex elliptic curve $E$, the Albanese kernel $T(E\times E)$ is generated, as an abelian group, by the exterior products \[ ([P]-[O])\times([Q]-[O]) \quad (P,Q\in E(\mathbb C)). \] Equivalently, the product map from $\mathrm{CH}_0(E)^0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathrm{CH}_0(E)^0$ onto $T(E\times E)$ is surjective. Products of algebraically trivial cycles are algebraically, and thus homologically and numerically, trivial; rational triviality is the false additional conclusion in question~25.

statement: A ring pair is henselian exactly when restriction preserves sections of every étale sheaf of sets, and then it preserves all cohomology degrees for every torsion abelian étale sheaf without noetherianity or invertibility of torsion.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:henselian} Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset A$ an ideal, with $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair; \item $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$ is bijective for every sheaf of sets on $X_{\acute et}$. \end{enumerate} Under these equivalent conditions, for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ and every integer $q\ge0$, restriction is an isomorphism \[ H^q_{\acute et}(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q_{\acute et}(Z,\mathcal F|_Z). \] No noetherian hypothesis or invertibility of the torsion orders is needed. In particular the assertion holds if $A\simeq\varprojlim_n A/I^n$, and for the henselization $A^h$ of $A$ along $I$.

statement: For a qcqs scheme pair, universal degree-zero étale comparison is equivalent to lifting clopen subsets of every finite cover and makes the global-function ring pair henselian, with full torsion comparison in the stated proper noetherian situation.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:henselian-general} Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $H^0(X,\mathcal F)\to H^0(Z,i^*\mathcal F)$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$; \item for every finite $X$-scheme $X'$, restriction induces a bijection between the clopen subsets of $X'$ and those of $X'\times_X Z$. \end{enumerate} Condition~(2) is the geometric definition of a \emph{henselian pair} $(X,Z)$. If these conditions hold, then \[ \bigl(B,J\bigr)=\bigl(\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X), \ker[\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)]\bigr) \] is a henselian ring pair. If, additionally, $X$ is proper over a noetherian ring $A$ and $Z=X\times_A A/I$ for some ideal $I\subset A$, the comparison is an isomorphism in every degree for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf on $X$.

statement: Universal degree-zero comparison for a scheme pair gives full faithfulness on finite étale covers and injectivity on all nonabelian H¹, and full torsion comparison is equivalent to vanishing in degrees at least two of all extension-by-zero torsion sheaves from the complement.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:H1-gate} Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be any closed immersion of schemes, and let $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ be its complement. Assume that $H^0(X,\mathcal F)\to H^0(Z,i^*\mathcal F)$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$. Then restriction is fully faithful on finite \'etale covers and is injective on the nonabelian pointed sets $H^1(X,G)\to H^1(Z,i^*G)$ for every \'etale sheaf of groups $G$. Moreover the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item restriction is an isomorphism in every degree for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf on $X$; \item $H^q(X,j_!\mathcal G)=0$ for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U$ and every $q\ge2$. \end{enumerate} The analogous vanishings in degrees zero and one already follow from the hypothesis. In particular the full torsion comparison holds whenever the torsion \'etale cohomological dimension of $X$ is at most one. None of these assertions needs quasi-compactness.

statement: For a qcqs pair satisfying universal degree-zero comparison, vanishing of H² for all complementary extension-by-zero torsion sheaves is equivalent to surjective torsion H¹ restriction and to lifting constant prime-power torsors on finite covers, and implies injective H² restriction.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:torsion-degree-two-reduction} Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion, and let $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ be its open complement. Assume that \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F) \] is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $H^2(X,j_!\mathcal G)=0$ for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U$. \item For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$, restriction on $H^1$ is surjective, and hence bijective. \item For every finite morphism $f:Y\to X$, every prime $\ell$, and every integer $\nu>0$, every torsor under the constant group $\mathbb Z/\ell^\nu\mathbb Z$ on $Y\times_XZ$ is the restriction of such a torsor on $Y$. \end{enumerate} In condition~(3), it suffices to test finite morphisms of finite presentation. If these conditions hold, restriction on $H^2$ is injective for every torsion abelian sheaf on $X$.

statement: A flat separated finite-type scheme over a henselian DVR is proper if every closed point lies in the special fibre, hence in particular under universal degree-zero étale comparison, without excellence or completeness.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:henselian-flat-trait-proper} Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring, with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, generic point $\eta$ and closed point $s$. Let $X$ be a flat separated scheme of finite type over $R$. Assume that restriction \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^0(X_s,\mathcal F|_{X_s}) \] is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$. Then $X$ is proper over $R$. Neither excellence nor completeness of $R$ is required. The same conclusion holds under the weaker hypothesis that every closed point of $X$ lies in $X_s$.

statement: A separated finite-type scheme over a henselian DVR satisfying universal degree-zero comparison with its special fibre has full torsion étale cohomology comparison without flatness or properness assumptions.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:henselian-trait-comparison} Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring, let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $R$, and put $Z=X_s$. Assume the universal degree-zero comparison for $(X,Z)$. Then, for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ and every $q\ge0$, \[ H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F). \] No flatness or properness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

statement: A separated finite-type scheme over a henselian ring pair is proper when its closed fibre is proper and the pair has universal degree-zero comparison, yielding full torsion comparison over a noetherian base.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:henselian-proper-closed-fibre} Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian ring pair and let $X$ be separated and of finite type over $A$. Put $Z=X\times_A A/I$. If $Z$ is proper over $A/I$ and $(X,Z)$ satisfies the universal degree-zero comparison, then $X$ is proper over $A$. If $A$ is noetherian, the all-degree torsion comparison of Theorem~\ref{B:henselian-general} follows.

statement: A flat separated finite-type scheme over a positive-dimensional henselian noetherian local ring is proper when every closed point lies in its closed fibre, and universal degree-zero comparison then gives all-degree torsion comparison.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:henselian-local-flat-proper} Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a henselian noetherian local ring with $\dim R>0$. Let $X$ be flat, separated and of finite type over $R$. If every point closed in $X$ belongs to the closed fibre $X_k$, then $X$ is proper over $R$. In particular, universal degree-zero comparison for $(X,X_k)$ implies properness and, for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ and every $q\geq0$, \[ H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim} H^q(X_k,\mathcal F|_{X_k}). \] No excellence, Nagata, reducedness, irreducibility, completeness, or dimension-one hypothesis is imposed on $R$.

statement: In a noetherian local domain, every nonzero nonunit is avoided by some prime whose quotient has dimension one.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:local-curve-avoidance} Let $(A,\mathfrak n)$ be a noetherian local domain and let $0\ne a\in\mathfrak n$. There is a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ such that $a\notin\mathfrak p$ and $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=1$.

statement: An integral separated finite-type scheme over a noetherian henselian pair with generic point outside the closed fibre is proper if all its closed points lie in that fibre, without locality, flatness, excellence, or finite-normalization assumptions.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:henselian-horizontal-proper} Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian ring pair with $A$ noetherian. Let $X$ be an integral separated scheme of finite type over $A$, whose generic point lies outside $X_I=X\times_A A/I$. If every point closed in $X$ belongs to $X_I$, then $X$ is proper over $A$. Locality of $A$, flatness, catenarity, excellence, normality, and a finite normalization hypothesis are not required.

statement: For a separated finite-type scheme over a noetherian henselian ring pair, containment of all closed points in the specified fibre implies all-degree torsion étale comparison, without flatness or properness.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:henselian-noetherian-pair-comparison} Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian ring pair with $A$ noetherian, let $X$ be any separated scheme of finite type over $A$, and set $Z=X\times_A A/I$. Suppose every closed point of $X$ lies in $Z$. Then for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ and every $q\ge0$, \[ H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim} H^q(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F). \] In particular this holds if $(X,Z)$ satisfies the universal degree-zero comparison for \'etale sheaves of sets. Neither flatness nor properness of $X$ is required. No locality, catenarity, excellence, completeness, or dimension hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

statement: For a separated finite-type scheme over a noetherian henselian pair, containment of every closed point in the specified fibre is equivalent to universal degree-zero comparison and therefore implies full torsion comparison.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:henselian-noetherian-closedpoint-criterion} Let $(A,I)$ be a noetherian henselian ring pair, let $X$ be separated and of finite type over $A$, and put $Z=X\times_A A/I$. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item every point closed in $X$ belongs to $Z$; \item restriction $H^0(X,\mathcal H)\to H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal H)$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal H$. \end{enumerate} Either condition therefore gives the all-degree torsion comparison of Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-noetherian-pair-comparison}.

statement: There exists a henselian normal local domain R with a nonzero nonunit d whose inversion gives the fraction field and a factorization d=ab for which neither factor nor its inverse belongs to R.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:Nagata-input} There are a normal local domain $(R,\mathfrak m)$, a nonzero $d\in\mathfrak m$, and $a,b\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ such that \[ R\text{ is henselian},\qquad R[1/d]=\operatorname{Frac}(R), \qquad ab=d, \qquad a,a^{-1},b,b^{-1}\notin R. \]

statement: The stated Nagata domain admits a normal local extension with two distinct branches separating a and b, making the open part V(d)∩D(a+b) of its closed divisor nonempty and disconnected.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:Goldman-branches} For $R,d,a,b$ as in Lemma~\ref{C:Nagata-input}, there is a normal local domain $(B,\mathfrak n)$ containing $R[a,b]$ such that \[ B[1/d]=\operatorname{Frac}(B),\qquad d\in\mathfrak n, \] and two primes $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak n$ satisfy \[ b\in\mathfrak p,\quad a\notin\mathfrak p, \qquad a\in\mathfrak q,\quad b\notin\mathfrak q. \] In particular $V(d)\cap D(a+b)$ is nonempty and disconnected in $\operatorname{Spec}B$.

statement: A qcqs scheme with a principal closed subscheme can satisfy universal degree-zero étale comparison while H¹ of every nontrivial finite constant cyclic group vanishes upstairs and is nonzero on the closed subscheme.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:subject21-torsion-counterexample} There exist a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $X$ and a principal closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ for which \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F) \quad\text{for every \'etale sheaf of sets }\mathcal F, \] but, for every integer $n>1$, \[ H^1(X,\underline{\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z})=0, \qquad H^1(Z,\underline{\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z})\ne0. \] In particular, degree-zero comparison for all \'etale sheaves of sets does not imply higher torsion comparison for arbitrary scheme pairs.

statement: A quasi-separated scheme satisfying universal degree-zero comparison with an affine closed subscheme is itself affine and consequently satisfies all-degree torsion comparison, without an initial quasi-compactness or noetherian hypothesis.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{C:henselian-affine-closed-fibre} Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be an affine closed subscheme. Suppose that \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F) \] is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets on $X$. Then $X$ is affine. Consequently restriction induces an isomorphism on $H^q$ for every $q\ge0$ and every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf on $X$. No quasi-compactness, noetherianity, or finite-presentation assumption on the original pair is required beyond the stated quasi-separatedness of $X$ and affineness of $Z$.

statement: For a qcqs pair with universal degree-zero comparison, henselizations of a finite affine neighborhood cover form an fpqc and v-cover with torsion cohomological descent, without ensuring that its Čech intersections are henselian pairs.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:henselized-affine-cover} Let $X$ be qcqs, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, and assume universal degree-zero comparison for every \'etale sheaf of sets. Choose finitely many affine open subschemes $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ whose union contains $Z$, and write $Z\cap U_a=\operatorname{Spec}(A_a/I_a)$. Then \[ W=\coprod_a\operatorname{Spec}(A_a)^h_{I_a}\longrightarrow X \] is an fpqc cover and a $v$-cover, with each displayed affine term a henselian pair along its inverse image of $Z$. Torsion \'etale cohomology satisfies descent along this cover. This statement does not assert that its \v Cech intersections are henselian pairs.

statement: For the displayed henselian k[[x,t]] pair, a henselized Čech self-intersection has a noninjective map on constant two-point sections and its further henselization is not an arc-cover, blocking automatic termwise henselian descent.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:henselized-Cech-obstruction} Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field and put \[ A=k[[x,t]],\qquad X=\operatorname{Spec}A,\qquad Z=V(t), \qquad B=(A[1/x])^h_{(t)}. \] The affine henselian pair $(X,Z)$ has universal degree-zero comparison. Nevertheless, with $C=B\otimes_A B$, the map \[ H^0(\operatorname{Spec}C,\{0,1\})\longrightarrow H^0(\operatorname{Spec}(C/tC),\{0,1\}) \] is not injective. Thus a \v Cech self-intersection in the henselization cover associated with $\{X,D(x)\}$ fails even the degree-zero hypothesis. Henselizing that intersection along $t$ does not produce an arc-cover of the original intersection. This refutes an automatic termwise descent argument, not torsion comparison for general henselian scheme pairs.

statement: The completion of C[x,y] along the displayed nodal cubic gives a noetherian henselian pair with regular integral ambient scheme and universal degree-zero comparison but H¹ of the constant integers changing from zero to Z, while torsion comparison remains valid.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:constant-integer-rigidity} Set \[ f=y^2-x^2(x+1),\qquad A=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\mathbb C[x,y]/(f^n),\qquad X=\operatorname{Spec}A,\quad Z=V(f)\subset X. \] Then $(A,fA)$ is a noetherian henselian pair, $X$ is regular and integral, and restriction on $H^0$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets. Nevertheless, for the constant abelian sheaf $\underline{\mathbb Z}$, \[ H^1_{\acute et}(X,\underline{\mathbb Z})=0, \qquad H^1_{\acute et}(Z,\underline{\mathbb Z})\simeq\mathbb Z. \] Thus the unrestricted-coefficient implication in subject~21 is false even for a constant, finitely generated, torsion-free coefficient group. For this very same pair, the comparison remains an isomorphism in all degrees for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf, by Theorem~\ref{B:henselian}.

statement: For C× and the point 1, the fixed sheaf μn has isomorphic degree-zero sections but different higher étale cohomology, so one-sheaf H⁰ agreement does not imply higher comparison.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:H0-counterexample} Even for an affine smooth complex scheme, an isomorphism in degree zero for a fixed torsion \'etale sheaf does not imply isomorphisms in higher degrees. Take $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[t,t^{-1}]$, $Z=\{t=1\}$ and $\mathcal F=\mu_n$ for any integer $n>1$.

statement: The henselized affine-line pair over C[[t]] has universal degree-zero comparison but fails H¹ comparison for the inverse-image additive structure sheaf, which differs from the closed fibre’s tensor-product structure sheaf.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:nontorsion-rigidity} Let $R=\mathbb C[[t]]$ and let $B=(R[x])^h_{(t)}$ be the henselization along the ideal $(t)$. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $i:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B/tB)\hookrightarrow X$, so $Z\simeq\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb C}$. Restriction is bijective on $H^0$ for every \'etale sheaf of sets on $X$. Nevertheless, for the additive \'etale structure sheaf $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, \[ H^1_{\acute et}(X,\mathcal F)=0, \qquad H^1_{\acute et}(Z,i^*\mathcal F)\ne0. \] Here $i^*\mathcal F$ means inverse image as an abelian \'etale sheaf, not the tensor-product structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Z$. Thus the literally unrestricted-sheaf reading of subject~21 is false, even for an affine henselian pair satisfying its strongest degree-zero hypothesis. The torsion theorem remains the valid replacement.

statement: For a henselian pair with finitely generated ideal, completion preserves torsion étale cohomology on the punctured spectrum, a comparison distinct from the affine closed-fibre rigidity theorem.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:Fujiwara} Let $(R,I)$ be a henselian pair, with $I$ finitely generated, let $\widehat R=\varprojlim R/I^n$, and put $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus V(I)$ and $\widehat U=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat R\setminus V(I\widehat R)$. For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U$, pullback induces a quasi-isomorphism \[ R\Gamma(U,\mathcal G)\simeq R\Gamma(\widehat U,\mathcal G|_{\widehat U}). \] This is the Fujiwara--Gabber punctured comparison. It is distinct from comparing an affine scheme with its closed fibre in Theorem~\ref{B:henselian}.

statement: The smooth elliptic family y²z=x³+txz²+z³ over F̄₅[[t]] has generic F₅-étale H¹ dimension one and special dimension zero, refuting full fundamental-group invariance while retaining prime-to-5 specialization invariance.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:specialization} Let $k=\overline{\mathbb F}_5$, $R=k[[t]]$, and let $\mathcal E/R$ be the projective Weierstrass curve with equation \[ y^2z=x^3+t xz^2+z^3. \] It is smooth and proper with geometrically connected fibres. If $\bar\eta$ is a geometric generic point and $0$ the closed point, then \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_5}H^1_{\acute et}(\mathcal E_{\bar\eta},\mathbb F_5)=1, \qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_5}H^1_{\acute et}(\mathcal E_0,\mathbb F_5)=0. \] Thus the specialization homomorphism of full \'etale fundamental groups cannot be an isomorphism. The general valid replacement for a smooth proper family with geometrically connected fibres is surjectivity, with an isomorphism on maximal prime-to-$p$ quotients when the specialization has residue characteristic $p$.

statement: The ordinary curve y²=x³−x and supersingular curve y²=x³+1 over F̄₅ have the same genus one but constant-F₅ Euler characteristics zero and one, so genus alone does not determine p-primary Euler characteristic.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:p-Euler} In characteristic $5$, the compactly supported Euler characteristic with constant $\mathbb F_5$ coefficients is not determined by the genus alone, even for smooth projective curves. Explicitly, over $\overline{\mathbb F}_5$, \[ E_{\mathrm{ord}}:y^2=x^3-x, \qquad E_{\mathrm{ss}}:y^2=x^3+1 \] have genus $1$, whereas $\chi(E_{\mathrm{ord}},\mathbb F_5)=0$ and $\chi(E_{\mathrm{ss}},\mathbb F_5)=1$. Thus one cannot answer subject 3 by replacing $\ell\ne p$ by $\ell=p$ in the usual genus-and-Swan formula without additional invariants or hypotheses.

statement: Étale abelian sheaves have the same cohomology after inverse image to the big fppf site, and the stated proper smooth divided-power setting computes crystalline cohomology by the coherent de Rham complex of its connection.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject1} For a scheme $X$, an abelian sheaf $F$ on its small \'etale site, and every $q\ge0$, the canonical change-of-topology map gives \[ H^q_{\acute et}(X,F)\simeq H^q_{\mathrm{fppf}}(X,F_{\mathrm{fppf}}). \] Here $F_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ is the inverse-image sheaf on the big flat site; this is not an assertion about arbitrary flat sheaves. A precise crystalline companion is the following. Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided-power ring, $A$ noetherian and $p$-adically complete, with $p$ nilpotent in $A/I$. If $Y/A$ is proper smooth, $X=Y_{A/I}$, and $\mathcal E$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent crystal on $X/A$, then it determines a coherent module with integrable connection $(E_Y,\nabla)$ and \[ R\Gamma(\operatorname{Cris}(X/A),\mathcal E) \simeq R\Gamma(Y,E_Y\otimes\Omega^\bullet_{Y/A}). \]

statement: Finite commutative groups over local function fields satisfy perfect degree-two flat Pontryagin duality, and finite flat groups on proper curves over finite fields satisfy degree-three finite duality, with compact support for open curves.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject2} Let $K$ be a local function field of characteristic $p$, and $N/K$ a finite commutative group scheme with Cartier dual $N^D$. With the canonical locally compact topologies, cup product gives perfect Pontryagin pairings \[ H^r_{\mathrm{fppf}}(K,N^D)\times H^{2-r}_{\mathrm{fppf}}(K,N) \longrightarrow\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z. \] Let $C$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over a finite field and $N/C$ finite flat commutative. There are perfect pairings of finite groups \[ H^r_{\mathrm{fppf}}(C,N^D)\times H^{3-r}_{\mathrm{fppf}}(C,N) \longrightarrow\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z. \] For an open curve the second factor is compactly supported flat cohomology, with the topologies specified in the source.

statement: Under the specified ordinary Galois-cover and pro-p monodromy hypotheses, p-coefficient curve sheaves satisfy Pink’s Euler formula with his local terms, while finite étale p-group covers have multiplicative compactly supported Qp Euler characteristic.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject3} Let $X/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, or a local field of residue characteristic $p$, and let $F$ be a constructible \'etale sheaf of finite-dimensional $\mathbb F$-vector spaces. Assume there is a finite irreducible Galois cover $Y\to X$ with $Y$ ordinary and the generic monodromy of the pullback of $F$ pro-$p$. Then \[ \chi(X,F)=(1-g_X)\operatorname{rank}F+ \sum_{x\in X(k)}\bigl(\dim F_x-\operatorname{LT}_x(F_{\bar\eta})\bigr). \] Here $\operatorname{LT}$ is Pink's local term, specified below. Without ordinariness there is no formula obtained merely by using the usual prime-to-$p$ genus term: Corollary~\ref{B:p-Euler} gives two genus-one counterexamples. Independently, a finite \'etale Galois cover $V\to U$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with $p$-group Galois group satisfies \[ \chi_c(V,\mathbb Q_p)=(\deg V/U)\chi_c(U,\mathbb Q_p). \]

statement: A lisse prime-to-characteristic ℓ-adic sheaf on a smooth separated variety has a boundary Swan zero-cycle whose degree corrects rank times Euler characteristic, recovering usual Swan conductors for curves and degree multiplicativity for proper finite étale covers.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject4} Let $U$ be a connected smooth separated scheme of finite type over a perfect field $k$, and let $\ell$ be invertible in $k$. For a lisse $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$-sheaf $F$ there is a rational Swan zero-cycle class on the boundary, in the inverse limit of the Chow groups of compactification boundaries, such that \[ \chi_c(U_{\bar k},F)=\operatorname{rank}(F)\chi_c(U_{\bar k},\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell) -\deg\operatorname{Sw}(F). \] For a smooth curve its degree is the sum of the usual Swan conductors. In particular a finite \'etale cover $V\to X$ of degree $d$ of smooth proper $k$-schemes satisfies $\chi(V_{\bar k},\mathbb Q_\ell)=d\chi(X_{\bar k},\mathbb Q_\ell)$.

statement: An abelian scheme on an open smooth curve with semisimple endomorphism-algebra action satisfies the representation-valued Euler formula obtained by decomposing its Tate module and weighting boundary Swan conductors of the multiplicity sheaves.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject5} Let $U$ be a smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, let $C$ be its smooth projective completion, and let $A/U$ be an abelian scheme. Fix $\ell\ne p$ and a finite-dimensional semisimple $\mathbb Q$-algebra $R$ acting on $A$. Put $V=T_\ell(A)\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$. After decomposing the split algebra $R\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$, write \[ V=\bigoplus_\rho W_\rho\otimes M_\rho, \] where $W_\rho$ are its distinct simple modules and $M_\rho$ are lisse multiplicity sheaves. In its representation Grothendieck group, \[ \sum_i(-1)^i[H_c^i(U,V)] =\chi_c(U,\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell)[V_{\bar\eta}] -\sum_{x\in C\setminus U}\sum_\rho\operatorname{Sw}_x(M_\rho)[W_\rho]. \]

statement: The finite-field Frobenius trace formula expresses compactly supported cohomological trace as a sum over rational points, and the compact complex holomorphic Lefschetz formula expresses coherent trace through nondegenerate fixed-point determinants.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject6} For a separated finite-type $X/\mathbb F_q$, a constructible $\mathbb Q_\ell$-sheaf $F$ with $\ell\nmid q$, and geometric Frobenius $\Phi$, \[ \sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi\mid H_c^i(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},F)) =\sum_{x\in X(\mathbb F_q)}\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi_x\mid F_{\bar x}). \] For a compact complex manifold $M$, a holomorphic $f:M\to M$ with only fixed points satisfying $\det_{\mathbb C}(1-df_x)\ne0$, a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ and a lift $u:f^*E\to E$, \[ \sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{Tr}(f,u\mid H^q(M,E)) =\sum_{f(x)=x}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(u_x)}{\det_{\mathbb C}(1-df_x)}. \]

statement: Bloch’s dualizing cycle complex gives torsion arithmetic duality over rings of integers and finite perfect Ext–compact-cohomology pairings for constructible sheaves, with Tate-modified real places.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject7} Let $B$ be the spectrum of the ring of integers of a number field and let $f:X\to B$ be separated of finite type. Let $\mathbb Z_X^c$ denote Bloch's dualizing cycle complex. For a torsion \'etale sheaf $F$ on $X$ there is a natural duality \[ R\operatorname{Hom}_X(F,\mathbb Z_X^c) \simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(R\Gamma_c(X,F),\mathbb Z)[-1]. \] For constructible $F$ it induces perfect finite pairings \[ \operatorname{Ext}^{2-i}_X(F,\mathbb Z_X^c)\times H_c^i(X,F) \longrightarrow\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z. \] At real places compact support is understood with the source's Tate modification.

statement: Holomorphic vector bundles with integrable connection correspond tensorially to local systems and satisfy de Rham duality on compact manifolds, while algebraic D-module and divided-power crystal descriptions require their stated characteristic and quasi-nilpotence hypotheses.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject8} Let $M$ be a complex manifold. Holomorphic finite-rank vector bundles with integrable connection are equivalent to finite-dimensional complex local systems, compatibly with tensor products, duals and internal Hom. If $M$ is compact of complex dimension $d$, the associated de Rham groups have perfect pairings \[ H^i_{\mathrm{dR}}(M,E)\times H^{2d-i}_{\mathrm{dR}}(M,E^\vee) \longrightarrow\mathbb C. \] For a smooth scheme in characteristic zero an integrable connection is the same as a left module structure over the sheaf of differential operators on the underlying vector bundle. In the divided-power characteristic-$p$ situation of subject~1, the crystal--connection correspondence additionally requires topological quasi-nilpotence.

statement: Complex analytic spaces countable at infinity and of bounded dimension admit dualizing complexes whose coherent cohomology and compact Ext groups are perfect strong topological duals after Hausdorff separation, reducing to finite-dimensional duality when compact.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject9} Let $X$ be a complex analytic space, countable at infinity and of bounded dimension. There is a dualizing complex $K_X$ and trace such that, for a coherent sheaf $F$, the separated quotients of \[ H^p(X,F)\quad\hbox{and}\quad\operatorname{Ext}^{-p}_c(X;F,K_X) \] are perfect strong topological duals in the canonical quotient-Fr\'echet and quotient-DFS topologies. Similarly $H_c^p(X,F)$ is dual to $\operatorname{Ext}^{-p}(X;F,K_X)$ after separation. When $X$ is compact, these are the usual finite-dimensional perfect pairings.

statement: The stated algebraic Riemann–Roch transformations commute with proper pushforward and tensor products, extend to projective lci perfect-complex classes in rational graded K-theory, and have an analytic proper-covariant K-homology counterpart.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject10} For a quasi-projective scheme $X$ over a field, there is a natural transformation $\tau_X:G_0(X)\to\mathrm{CH}_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, covariant for proper morphisms, satisfying \[ \tau_X(E\otimes F)=\operatorname{ch}(E)\cap\tau_X(F), \qquad \tau_X(\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cap[X] \] when respectively $E$ is a vector bundle and $X$ is smooth. More generally, for a projective local-complete-intersection morphism $f:X\to Y$ of constant virtual relative dimension, where $Y$ is quasi-compact with an ample line bundle, SGA~6 gives \[ \operatorname{ch}(f_!x)=f_{\mathrm{gr},*} \bigl(\operatorname{ch}(x)\operatorname{td}(T_f)\bigr) \] in the rational associated graded of $K$-theory, for perfect-complex classes $x$. For complex analytic spaces there is a proper-covariant transformation from coherent $G_0$ to topological $K$-homology, agreeing with the usual bundle class under Poincar\'e identification on a complex manifold.

statement: Every abelian variety over a discretely valued field has a smooth separated finite-type Néron model uniquely representing extension of maps from smooth schemes over the valuation ring.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject11} Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $K$ its fraction field, and $A/K$ an abelian variety. The functor on smooth $R$-schemes \[ T\longmapsto\operatorname{Hom}_K(T_K,A) \] is represented by a smooth separated group scheme $\mathcal A/R$ of finite type. Its generic fibre is $A$ and its representing property characterizes it up to unique isomorphism.

statement: An abelian variety over the function field of a connected Dedekind scheme has a smooth separated finite-type Néron model agreeing with any abelian-scheme extension on its domain of existence.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject12} Let $S$ be a connected Dedekind scheme, $K$ its function field and $A/K$ an abelian variety. There is a smooth separated finite-type $S$-group scheme $\mathcal A$ with generic fibre $A$, satisfying \[ \operatorname{Hom}_S(T,\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(T_K,A) \] for every smooth $S$-scheme $T$. On an open set on which $A$ extends to an abelian scheme, that abelian scheme is its N\'eron model.

statement: Finite-type schemes over the specified henselian DVRs have linear Greenberg approximation, and polynomial systems over excellent henselian noetherian local rings have arbitrary-order approximation of formal solutions.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject13} Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $t$, and assume $\widehat K/K$ is separable if the fraction field $K$ has positive characteristic. For a finite-type $R$-scheme $X$ there is a linear function $\beta(n)=an+b$ such that any point modulo $t^{\beta(n)}$ has the same reduction modulo $t^n$ as some point of $X(R)$. In particular \[ X(R)\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X(R/t^n)\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }n. \] For an excellent henselian noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, every finite system of polynomial equations over $R$ with a solution in $\widehat R$ has solutions in $R$ congruent to it modulo any prescribed $\mathfrak m^n$.

statement: For noetherian local rings, excellence plus henselianity is equivalent to approximation and strong approximation, although the approximation function need not have a linear bound even over Q[[s,t]].
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:strong-approximation} For a noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, the following three conditions are equivalent: $R$ is excellent and henselian; $R$ has the approximation property; and $R$ has the strong approximation property. Here approximation means that every solution in $\widehat R$ of a finite polynomial system over $R$ can be approximated to every finite order by a solution in $R$. Strong approximation means that, for each $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\in R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_N]^r$, there is a function $\beta:\mathbb N_{>0}\to\mathbb N_{>0}$ such that \[ f(a)\in(\mathfrak m^{\beta(n)})^r \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \exists b\in R^N:\ f(b)=0,\quad b-a\in(\mathfrak m^n)^N. \] In particular every complete noetherian local ring has strong approximation. The function need not admit a linear bound, even for $R=\mathbb Q[[s,t]]$.

statement: For U²−V²W over Q[[s,t]], the displayed truncations have error order m²−4 but no exact zero within order 2m−2, forcing quadratic lower growth and excluding a linear Artin approximation bound.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:nonlinear-Artin} In $R=\mathbb Q[[s,t]]$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=(s,t)$, put $f(U,V,W)=U^2-V^2W$. For every integer $m\ge5$, set \[ \begin{split} u_m&=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}{\binom{1/2}{j}} s^{2m-2-2j}t^{(m-2)j},\\ v_m&=s^{2m-3},\qquad w_m=s^2+t^{m-2}. \end{split} \] Then $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak m}f(u_m,v_m,w_m)=m^2-4$, but no exact zero of $f$ is congruent to $(u_m,v_m,w_m)$ modulo $\mathfrak m^{2m-2}$. Hence every function $\beta$ in Theorem~\ref{B:strong-approximation} for this $f$ satisfies \[ \beta(2m-2)>m^2-4\qquad(m\ge5), \] so no linear bound exists.

statement: A topos with a finite-limit site and finite refinements of covers has enough points, and smooth algebraic-space groupoids present precisely algebraic stacks through their quotient stacks and smooth atlases.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject14} A topos admitting a site with finite limits and with a finite subcover refining every covering has enough points. Also, if $R\rightrightarrows U$ is a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces, its quotient stack $[U/R]$ is algebraic. Conversely an algebraic stack with a smooth atlas $U$ has the presentation $[U/(U\times_{\mathcal X}U)]$.

statement: The sheaf topos on the complete Boolean algebra of regular open subsets of R is nondegenerate but has no geometric point or finite-limit-and-colimit-preserving set-valued fibre functor.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:pointless} Let $B$ be the complete Boolean algebra of regular open subsets of $\mathbb R$, where $U$ is regular open if $U=\operatorname{int}\overline U$. Regard $B$ as a site whose covers of $U$ are families with join $U$. The Grothendieck topos $\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ is nondegenerate and has no geometric point $\operatorname{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(B)$. In particular it has no set-valued fibre functor that preserves finite limits and all colimits.

statement: Every Grothendieck topos has a surjective geometric morphism from sheaves on a complete Boolean algebra, whose conservative left-exact inverse image is comonadic and provides a Boolean-valued reconstruction even without points.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:Boolean-localization} For every Grothendieck topos $\mathcal E$, there are a complete Boolean algebra $B$ and a surjective geometric morphism \[ p:\operatorname{Sh}(B)\longrightarrow\mathcal E. \] Equivalently, $p^*:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ preserves finite limits and all colimits and is conservative. It is comonadic, so $\mathcal E$ is recovered as the category of coalgebras for its induced comonad. This gives a universal Boolean-valued replacement for ordinary fibre functors even when $\mathcal E$ has no points.

statement: A pointed connected simplicial set has a universal schematic homotopy type with proalgebraic fundamental group and the stated characteristic-zero higher groups, while proper schemes over henselian pairs share their closed fibre’s profinite étale homotopy type.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject15} For every field $k$ and pointed connected simplicial set $T$, there is a schematization $(T\otimes k)^{\mathrm{sch}}$, characterized by the universal map from $T$ to a pointed schematic homotopy type. Its fundamental group is the affine proalgebraic completion of $\pi_1(T)$; for simply connected finite-type $T$ in characteristic zero its higher homotopy groups are the additive group schemes of $\pi_i(T)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}k$. Separately, for a henselian pair $(A,I)$ and a proper $X/A$, the closed fibre $Z=X_{A/I}$ has the same profinite \'etale homotopy type as $X$.

statement: A polynomial pointed simplicial affine scheme over F₂ can be degreewise smooth and Kan on every algebra while its rational-point π₂ is Z/4 and its normalized tangent-complex H₂ is (Z/2)², refuting the proposed Lie comparison.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:Lie-comparison-counterexample} There is a pointed simplicial affine scheme \(X_\bullet\) over \(k=\mathbf F_2\) such that \[ X_0=X_1=\operatorname{Spec}k, \qquad X_n\simeq\mathbf A_k^{\,2\binom n2}, \] all simplicial structure maps are pointed polynomial maps, and \(X_\bullet(R)\) is Kan for every commutative \(k\)-algebra \(R\), but \[ \pi_2\bigl(X_\bullet(k)\bigr)\simeq\mathbf Z/4\mathbf Z, \qquad H_2\bigl(N\operatorname{Lie}X_\bullet\bigr) \simeq(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2. \] Here \(N\) denotes the normalized chain complex. In particular, the left group admits no \(k\)-module structure, and the comparison cannot hold even as an isomorphism of abelian groups.

statement: A polynomial pointed simplicial affine scheme over Z can be Kan on every ring with integral-point π₂=Z but tangent-complex H₂=Z⊕Z/2, so restricting the proposed smooth Kan Lie comparison to Z does not repair it.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:Lie-comparison-integral-counterexample} There is a pointed simplicial affine scheme \(Y_\bullet\) over \(\mathbf Z\) with \[ Y_0=Y_1=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z, \qquad Y_n\simeq\mathbf A_{\mathbf Z}^{\,2\binom n2+\binom n3}, \] polynomial structure maps, and a Kan simplicial set \(Y_\bullet(R)\) for every commutative ring \(R\), such that \[ \pi_2\bigl(Y_\bullet(\mathbf Z)\bigr)\simeq\mathbf Z, \qquad H_2\bigl(N\operatorname{Lie}Y_\bullet\bigr) \simeq\mathbf Z\oplus\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z. \] Thus restricting the displayed comparison of \S118 to \(k=\mathbf Z\) does not repair its stated smooth Kan sufficient conditions.

statement: The specified integral affine-stack construction on simply connected spaces with finitely generated homotopy groups has Hilbert-group-valued homotopy sheaves, retracts on integer points and mapping spaces, and preserves equivalence while its integer-point homotopy includes the stated prime-completion correction.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:integral-affinization} Let $T$ be a pointed simply connected space with every $\pi_i(T)$, $i\ge2$, finitely generated. Work in hypercomplete fpqc stacks on affine schemes over $\mathbf Z$. Let affine stacks mean the full subcategory generated by the $K(\mathbf G_a,n)$ under small homotopy limits, and put \[ F_T=(T\otimes\mathbf Z)^{\mathrm{uni}} =\mathbf R\operatorname{Spec}C^*(T,\mathbf Z),\qquad \mathbb H=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbf Z). \] Here $C^*$ is the cosimplicial commutative cochain ring, and $\operatorname{Int}(\mathbf Z)=\{P\in\mathbf Q[x]:P(\mathbf Z)\subset\mathbf Z\}$, with the additive Hopf structure. Then $F_T$ is universal for maps from $T$ to integer-valued points of affine stacks, and \[ \pi_i(F_T)\simeq\pi_i(T)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbb H\quad(i\ge2) \] as fpqc abelian sheaves; these sheaves have natural $\mathbb H$-module structures. The unit $u_T:T\to F_T(\mathbf Z)$ has a natural retraction. The induced map of mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}(T,S)\to\operatorname{Map}(F_T,F_S)$ also has a retraction for every $S$ in this class, and $F_T\simeq F_S$ if and only if $T\simeq S$. At the induced basepoint, \[ \pi_i(F_T(\mathbf Z))\simeq \pi_i(T)\oplus\prod_{p\text{ prime}}\widehat{\pi_{i+1}(T)}_p \qquad(i\ge1). \] The homotopy sheaves need not be $\mathcal O$-modules, and the unit need not be a weak equivalence. These assertions concern this specified integral affine-stack construction, without identifying it with the unspecified infinitesimal enrichment in the 1964 sheet.

statement: The derived global-functions affine-stack construction gives universal unipotent homotopy groups, the unipotent-bundle Tannaka group in degree one, coherent-Hurewicz comparisons, and in proper positive characteristic the stated profinite and pro-p étale comparisons.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:unipotent-homotopy} Let $k$ be a field. A higher stack here is a sheaf of spaces for the fpqc topology on affine $k$-schemes. An affine stack is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B$ belongs to the homotopy theory of cosimplicial commutative $k$-algebras. For a pointed higher stack $(X,x)$ such that $k\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$, put \[ \mathbf U(X)=\operatorname{Spec}R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X),\qquad \pi_i^{\mathrm U}(X,x)=\pi_i(\mathbf U(X),x)\quad(i\ge1). \] The derived algebra structure, including its cosimplicial commutative operations, is part of this definition. Then the following hold. \begin{enumerate} \item The map $X\to\mathbf U(X)$ is universal for maps to affine stacks. The stack $\mathbf U(X)$ is connected and hypercomplete, and its $\pi_i^{\mathrm U}$ are represented by unipotent affine group schemes, commutative for $i\ge2$. Here unipotent means that every nonzero finite-dimensional representation has a nonzero invariant vector. Finite type of these group schemes is not required. \item If $X$ is a scheme of finite type over $k$ and $x\in X(k)$, then $\pi_1^{\mathrm U}(X,x)$ is naturally the Tannaka group of the category of unipotent vector bundles on $X$, with fibre functor $x^*$. Here a unipotent vector bundle has a finite filtration by subbundles whose successive quotients are trivial line bundles. This is the unipotent Nori fundamental group in this specified sense. \item For every integer $r\ge1$, \[ H^j(X,\mathcal O_X)=0\ (1\le j\le r) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_j^{\mathrm U}(X,x)=1\ (1\le j\le r). \] Under these equivalent conditions there are natural maps \[ H^{r+1}(X,\mathcal O_X) \simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_{r+1}^{\mathrm U}(X,x),\mathbf G_a), \qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1(\pi_{r+1}^{\mathrm U}(X,x),\mathbf G_a) \hookrightarrow H^{r+2}(X,\mathcal O_X). \] The extension group is for commutative fpqc group sheaves; the restriction $r\ge1$ ensures that its first argument is commutative. \item If $X$ is a proper $k$-scheme and $k$ has characteristic $p>0$, every $\pi_i^{\mathrm U}(X,x)$ is profinite. If moreover $k$ is algebraically closed, the comparison induced by $\mathbf F_p\to\mathcal O_X$ identifies its maximal pro-\'etale quotient with the affine group scheme associated to the pro-$p$-finite group \[ \pi_i\bigl(\operatorname{Et}(X)^{\wedge}_p,x\bigr). \] Here $\operatorname{Et}(X)^{\wedge}_p$ is the pro-$p$-finite completion of the entire \'etale homotopy type. The displayed group retains its profinite topology. Still assuming $k$ algebraically closed, if Frobenius acts bijectively on every $H^j(X,\mathcal O_X)$, these comparison maps are themselves isomorphisms. \end{enumerate} These conclusions concern a specified theory of schemes and higher stacks. They make no identification with the unspecified infinitesimal enrichment of the 1964 thesis sheet.

statement: With coherent cohomology vanishing below n and in degree n+1 and finite dimension in degree n, the nth unipotent homotopy group has a formal Lie dual of that dimension, which for proper schemes over algebraically closed positive-characteristic fields represents the stated Artin–Mazur functor and has the indicated Witt-cohomology Dieudonné module.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:formal-homotopy} Let $k$ be a field, let $n\geq2$, and let $X$ be a pointed higher stack for the fpqc topology on affine $k$-schemes. Use the affine-stack construction \[ \mathbf U(X)=\operatorname{Spec}R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O), \qquad G=\pi_n^{\mathrm U}(X)=\pi_n(\mathbf U(X)), \] where $R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O)$ retains its cosimplicial commutative algebra structure, in the category used in Theorem~\ref{B:unipotent-homotopy}. Suppose that \[ \begin{gathered} H^0(X,\mathcal O)=k,\qquad H^i(X,\mathcal O)=0\quad(0<i<n),\\ g=\dim_k H^n(X,\mathcal O)<\infty, \qquad H^{n+1}(X,\mathcal O)=0. \end{gathered} \] Then $G$ is a commutative affine unipotent group scheme and its dual $G^\vee$ is a commutative formal Lie group of dimension $g$. Here the dual is defined by the linearly compact topological Hopf algebra $\mathcal O(G)^*$, with the topology dual to the finite-dimensional subcoalgebras of $\mathcal O(G)$; the conclusion includes an isomorphism of its underlying topological algebra with $k[[t_1,\ldots,t_g]]$. If, in addition, $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$ and $X$ is a proper $k$-scheme with a chosen $k$-point, let $\operatorname{Art}_k$ be the category of local Artinian $k$-algebras with specified residue identification $A/\mathfrak m_A=k$. The covariant functor $\Phi_X^n:\operatorname{Art}_k\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is defined by \[ \Phi_X^n(A)=\ker\!\left( H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathbf G_m) \longrightarrow H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathbf G_m)\right) \qquad(A\in\operatorname{Art}_k) \] and is represented by the formal Lie group $G^\vee$. In particular, \[ \Phi_X^n\simeq (\pi_n^{\mathrm U}(X))^\vee, \qquad \mathbf M(\Phi_X^n) \simeq \varprojlim_r H^n_{\mathrm{Zar}}(X,W_r), \] where $W_r$ denotes the length-$r$ $p$-typical Witt-vector group and $\mathbf M$ is the formal-group Dieudonn\'e functor in the convention specified below. Smoothness, projectivity, ordinarity and finite formal-group height are not needed for this comparison.

statement: Full étale fundamental groups need not be invariant in smooth proper curve families, but specialization is surjective with prime-to-p invariance and the stated away-from-residue-characteristic étale homotopy comparison.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject16} The blanket assertion that full \'etale fundamental groups are invariant in smooth proper curve families is false, even for the explicit genus-one family of Proposition~\ref{B:specialization}. For such families over a trait of residue characteristic $p$, specialization is surjective and induces an isomorphism on maximal prime-to-$p$ quotients. At the homotopy level, after completion away from the residue characteristics, the geometric fibres of a smooth proper morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes have equivalent \'etale homotopy types under specialization.

statement: For a pointed smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field, Nori’s profinite affine group classifies pointed torsors under each fixed finite group scheme and its maximal pro-étale quotient recovers the usual étale fundamental group.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:nori-finite-flat} Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve, and fix $x\in X(k)$. There is a profinite affine $k$-group scheme $\pi^{\mathrm N}(X,x)$ such that, for every finite $k$-group scheme $G$, homomorphisms \[ \pi^{\mathrm N}(X,x)\longrightarrow G \] classify isomorphism classes of pointed fppf $G$-torsors $(P,p)$ on $(X,x)$, with the structure group $G$ fixed. Restricting this classification to finite \'etale $G$ recovers the usual pointed finite \'etale torsors, so the maximal pro-\'etale quotient is the constant pro-group scheme associated with $\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,x)$.

statement: The displayed ordinary genus-two curve over F̄₂ has a Nori fundamental group whose canonical base-change map to the algebraic closure of F̄₂(t) is not an isomorphism.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:nori-base-change-counterexample} Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_2$, choose $\alpha\in\mathbf F_4\subset k$ with $\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0$, and let $X/k$ be the smooth projective model of \[ y^2+x(x+1)y=x(x+1)(x^3+\alpha x+\alpha). \] Choose any $x_0\in X(k)$ and put $K=\overline{k(t)}$. Then $X$ is an ordinary curve of genus $2$, but the canonical map \[ \pi^{\mathrm N}(X_K,x_0)\longrightarrow \pi^{\mathrm N}(X,x_0)\times_k K \] is not an isomorphism.

statement: A proper flat finitely presented algebraic-space family with universally trivial relative global functions has a quasi-separated locally finitely presented Picard algebraic space, separated for geometrically integral fibres and smooth in relative dimension at most one.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:Picard-general} Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper flat finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces. Assume that $\mathcal O_T\to f_{T*}\mathcal O_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism for every scheme $T\to S$. Then the fppf sheaf $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ is an algebraic space, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation over $S$. It is separated if all geometric fibres of $f$ are integral, and smooth if $f$ has relative dimension at most one. No noetherian or one-dimensional hypothesis on the base is required.

statement: For a regular proper flat curve model over a strictly henselian DVR with perfect residue field, gcd one of special-fibre multiplicities is equivalent to separatedness and schematic representability of Pic⁰, and the appropriate separated Picard quotient yields the generic Jacobian’s Néron model.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject17} Let $R$ be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field, and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a proper flat regular model of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. Write the special fibre as $\sum_jm_jC_j$, and put $\delta=\gcd_jm_j$. Then \[ \delta=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/R}\text{ is representable by a scheme} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/R}\text{ is separated}. \] Moreover the appropriate separated quotient of the closure of the generic Picard identity component is the N\'eron model of the generic Jacobian.

statement: The free quotient of E×Spec C[[s]] by translation by nonzero two-torsion combined with s↦−s gives a regular proper flat genus-one family over t=s² whose Pic⁰ is nonseparated and nonschematic although its full Picard functor is an algebraic space.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:Picard-double-fibre} Let $R=\mathbb C[[t]]$, $R'=\mathbb C[[s]]$ with $t=s^2$, and let $E/\mathbb C$ be the elliptic curve $y^2=x^3-x$, with origin $O$ and two-torsion point $T=(0,0)$. The involution \[ (P,s)\longmapsto(P+T,-s) \] on $Y=E\times\operatorname{Spec}R'$ has a scheme quotient $X=Y/C_2$. The morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is proper, flat and finitely presented, its total space is regular, and its generic fibre is a smooth geometrically connected genus-one curve. Nevertheless $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/R}$ is not separated and is not representable by a scheme. The full Picard functor is represented by an algebraic space.

statement: Affine schemes have effective fpqc descent over arbitrary, including Artinian, bases, and a free finite locally free group action has an algebraic-space quotient with effective descended torsor data when that quotient is schematic.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject18} For any fpqc covering $\{S_i\to S\}$, every descent datum on schemes affine over $S_i$ is effective, with no noetherian assumption. In particular this applies over an Artinian base. If a finite locally free group scheme $G/S$ acts freely on an $S$-scheme $X$, the fppf quotient is an algebraic space; when that quotient is represented by a scheme, the descended $G$-torsor and its affine descent data are effective.

statement: The affine line with doubled origin over Q(i), with conjugation interchanging its two charts, has finite-étale descent data over the Artinian base Q that are ineffective in schemes and yield a nonschematic algebraic space.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:descent-counterexample} Let $k=\mathbb Q$, $L=\mathbb Q(i)$, and let $X/L$ be the affine line with doubled origin: glue two copies $U_+$ and $U_-$ of $\operatorname{Spec}L[t]$ by the identity on $D(t)$. The involution that conjugates $i$, fixes $t$, and interchanges the two charts gives a descent datum for the finite \'etale cover $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. This datum is not effective in schemes, although $X$ is smooth and of finite type over $L$ and the base $k$ is Artinian. Its quotient is an algebraic space that is not a scheme.

statement: A semilinear action for a finite Galois field extension has effective schematic descent exactly when the scheme admits a covering by invariant affine opens.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:descent-criterion} Let $L/k$ be a finite Galois extension and let an $L$-scheme $X$ carry a semilinear action of $G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)$. Its descent datum is effective in schemes if and only if $X$ has an open covering by $G$-stable affine subschemes.

statement: On a projective variety, pliant cones generated by globally generated Schur classes are full-dimensional and salient with ample complete intersections in their interiors and the stated pullback/product properties, while ample degree extends to a norm on numerical cycles.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject19} For a projective variety $X$ over an algebraically closed field, let $N^k(X)$ be the space of numerical codimension-$k$ classes. The pliant cone $\operatorname{PL}^k(X)$, generated and closed by products of Schur classes of globally generated vector bundles, is full dimensional and salient; ample complete intersections lie in its interior. These cones are stable under pullback, lie in the pseudoeffective cones and are stable under products. The pseudoeffective cone of $k$-cycles is full dimensional and salient, and degree against an ample class extends to a norm on the numerical cycle space.

statement: Dominant line bundles on the flag variety of a split semisimple simply connected group have vanishing higher cohomology in every characteristic with the globally generated sign convention.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject20} Let $G$ be a split semisimple simply connected algebraic group over a perfect field, $B$ a Borel subgroup, and $\lambda$ a dominant weight. With the convention that dominant weights define globally generated line bundles on $G/B$, \[ H^q(G/B,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0\qquad(q>0). \] The assertion holds in every characteristic.

statement: Universal degree-zero comparison characterizes qcqs henselian scheme pairs and yields full torsion comparison in the stated affine, proper, and separated finite-type noetherian settings, but arbitrary coefficients and arbitrary nonnoetherian nonseparated pairs admit the listed degree-one counterexamples.
statement_summary_status: one-sentence restatement checked against complete source statement; not itself a proof check
statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject21} For a quasi-compact quasi-separated closed pair, degree-zero comparison for every \'etale sheaf of sets is equivalent to geometric henselianity. In the affine case it implies comparison in every degree for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf; the same conclusion holds in the proper situation of Theorem~\ref{B:henselian-general}, and for every separated finite-type scheme over a henselian discrete valuation ring by Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-trait-comparison}. If $Z$ is affine and $X$ is quasi-separated, Proposition~\ref{C:henselian-affine-closed-fibre} forces $X$ to be affine and gives the same conclusion. Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-noetherian-pair-comparison} proves the torsion comparison for every separated finite-type scheme over any noetherian henselian ring pair $(A,I)$ with $Z=X\times_A A/I$, assuming only that every closed point of $X$ lies in $Z$. Corollary~\ref{C:henselian-noetherian-closedpoint-criterion} proves that, in this class, the closed-point condition is equivalent to universal degree-zero comparison. No flatness, locality, catenarity, excellence or properness of $X$ is required. Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-horizontal-proper} identifies the proper horizontal components; Theorem~\ref{B:henselian-local-flat-proper} remains a separate proof for flat positive-dimensional local bases. Completeness and henselization give the two affine cases named on scan~4. Completion of a punctured henselian pair with finitely generated ideal gives a second, distinct comparison. The affine and punctured statements extend to torsion sheaves of spaces, and consequently to the associated profinite \'etale homotopy types. The assertion with arbitrary abelian coefficients is false even for the constant integer sheaf on an affine henselian pair, by Proposition~\ref{B:constant-integer-rigidity}; Proposition~\ref{B:nontorsion-rigidity} supplies a separate coherent-sheaf example; the torsion implication for arbitrary closed pairs is also false: Theorem~\ref{C:subject21-torsion-counterexample} constructs a qcqs nonseparated nonnoetherian pair with universal degree-zero comparison but failure of degree-one comparison for every constant $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, $n>1$. statement: Chow homology has proper pushforward and flat pullback, morphisms from arbitrary pure quasi-projective sources to smooth targets give integral pullback classes, and regular finite-dimensional noetherian targets have rational intersection products compatible with Serre’s Tor formula.

statement_full_latex: \label{B:subject23} For schemes of finite type over a field, ordinary Chow homology admits proper pushforward and flat pullback. statement: Rational Chow classes on a regular separated finite-dimensional noetherian scheme inject canonically into operational Chow cohomology, giving functorial pullback operations on arbitrary finite-type sources without requiring their regularity.

statement_full_latex: \label{B:regular-pullback} Let $Y$ be a separated regular noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension. Consequently every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of finite type, with no regularity assumption on $X$, has canonical operations \[ f^*\widetilde\alpha\cap-: \mathrm{CH}_j(X)_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{j-p}(X)_{\mathbb Q} \quad(\alpha\in\mathrm{CH}^p(Y)_{\mathbb Q}). \] They commute with proper pushforward, flat pullback and refined Cartier-divisor intersection, and are functorial under further pullback as operational classes. Thus the regular-target assertion has an arbitrary-source rational form, including the ample-line-bundle setting of the manuscript.
